title: A multimodal CT-based machine-learning model for differentiating pulmonary sarcomatoid carcinoma from conventional non-small cell lung cancer: an internally validated study
abstract: Abstract Background: Pulmonary sarcomatoid carcinoma (PSC) is difficult to distinguish from conventional non-small cell lung cancer (c-NSCLC) before pathological diagnosis. We evaluated whether clinical–CT semantic features, radiomics and deep-learning features can support this distinction. Methods: After image quality control, 397 patients (83 PSC, 314 c-NSCLC) from three institutions were analysed. Six models (clinical-only, radiomics-only, deep-only, clinical+radiomics, clinical+deep and full fusion) were developed and evaluated with repeated nested cross-validation (five outer folds repeated 20 times, five inner folds), with preprocessing, feature selection, hyperparameter tuning, classifier selection and threshold selection confined to training folds. Discrimination, calibration and operating-point performance were estimated from patient-level out-of-fold predictions. The influence of CT acquisition heterogeneity was examined in sensitivity analyses. Results: The prespecified full fusion model achieved an AUROC of 0.890 (95% CI 0.848–0.930) and an AUPRC of 0.739 (0.643–0.823; PSC prevalence 0.209). At a training-derived high-sensitivity threshold, sensitivity and specificity were 0.855 and 0.755. The clinical+radiomics model performed similarly (AUROC 0.895, 0.851–0.934), the clinical-only model reached 0.843 (0.796–0.887), and deep features alone were not discriminative (AUROC 0.533). Intratumoral low-attenuation area (LAA) presence and LAA ratio were independently associated with PSC. Acquisition parameters alone also discriminated the groups (AUROC 0.901); after adjustment for acquisition variables, radiomics retained incremental value over clinical features (ΔAUROC 0.075, P<0.001), but residual confounding by source or protocol cannot be excluded. Conclusions: Intratumoral LAA features and CT radiomics may help flag PSC before pathology in an internally validated setting, whereas Kinetics-pretrained deep features added no value. Because acquisition heterogeneity may contribute to imaging-based performance and a negative prediction cannot exclude PSC, the model should be regarded as exploratory and requires external validation with standardized acquisition before clinical use.

title: Malnutrition-associated reversible splenial lesion syndrome after metabolic surgery: a case report
abstract: Abstract Background Reversible splenial lesion syndrome (RESLES) is a rare clinicoradiological entity characterized by an oval, reversible lesion in the splenium of the corpus callosum (SCC), with diagnosis relying primarily on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). The etiologic spectrum is wide and suggests a “final common pathway” triggered by diverse systemic insults. Metabolic surgery, while effective for weight reduction, can precipitate severe malnutrition and internal environmental perturbations. Here we report a case of RESLES associated with malnutrition after sleeve gastrectomy, which is rarely described in the literature. Case presentation A 14-year-old female with no previous neurological disorders presented with nausea, vomiting, and oliguria one month after undergoing sleeve gastrectomy. Persistent inadequate oral intake post-surgery led to severe malnutrition, dehydration, and acute kidney injury. Laboratory evaluation revealed profound electrolyte disturbances, specifically severe hypokalemia (nadir 2.52 mmol/L), and marked azotemia (creatinine 1451.3 µmol/L). Cranial MRI demonstrated an ovoid lesion (10 × 12 mm) in the SCC with isointensity on T1-weighted images, slight hyperintensity on T2-weighted images, and restricted diffusion on DWI, consistent with RESLES. After one month of intensive treatment—including hemodialysis, fluid resuscitation, electrolyte and vitamin supplementation, and anti-infective therapy—her symptoms resolved completely, and follow-up MRI showed total resolution of the lesion without neurological sequelae. Conclusions Metabolic and osmotic perturbations associated with malnutrition after metabolic surgery may trigger RESLES. Timely identification and correction of the underlying causes yield a favorable prognosis. Clinicians should maintain a high index of suspicion for RESLES in post-bariatric patients presenting with neurological symptoms.

title: A Novel Open-Set Domain Adaptation Framework for Histopathology Image Classification: A Style-Aware and Density-Guided Approach
abstract: Abstract In computational pathology, deployed histopathology models frequently encounter variations in staining protocols and scanning devices, as well as tissue categories that are absent from the training distribution. In this study, we address these challenges under the Open-Set Domain Adaptation (OSDA) setting, where a labeled source domain is adapted to an unlabeled target domain containing both known categories shared with the source domain and unknown tissue categories. We propose SADG, a Style-Aware and Density-Guided framework that jointly addresses covariate and semantic shifts. For semantic shift, unlike existing OSDA methods that collapse all unknown samples into a single category and overlook the intrinsic density structure of the target domain, a GMM-based ClusterNet models the density structure of target features and constructs class-conditional prototypes characterizing the distribution of shared known classes. Based on these cluster-guided statistics, a Gaussian Mixture-based Energy Measurement (GEM) score is derived to quantify sample openness and is further calibrated via Extreme Value Theory (EVT) to estimate unknown-class probabilities without fixed thresholds. To mitigate covariate shift, a Style Rectification Module (SRM) is incorporated into the backbone to suppress appearance-induced domain discrepancies while preserving diagnostically relevant style information. Furthermore, reliable homogeneous target clusters guide the classifier toward learning shared known classes, while pseudo-unknown samples prevent unknown instances from collapsing into known-class regions. Experiments on the Kather-16 and Kather-19 colorectal histopathology datasets under three open-set configurations demonstrate that SADG consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both known-class classification and unknown-class detection. Code is available at https://github.com/ReyhaneGhaffari/SADG-OSDA.git.

title: An acoustic coupling fluid improves intraoperative ultrasound image quality during glioma surgery: Results of a Pivotal Multicenter Study (NCT04734444)
abstract: Abstract Intraoperative ultrasound uniquely provides repeatable, real-time guidance throughout glioma resection without interrupting surgery. However, image quality deteriorates at resection completion, when imaging is most critical: irrigation fluids attenuate ultrasound less than brain tissue, producing hyperechoic artefacts beneath the cavity that obscure or mimic residual tumour. Existing operator-dependent strategies do not correct this mismatch. Here, we show that SonoClear, a tissue-mimicking acoustic coupling fluid, reduces these artefacts and improves interpretability. In a prospective, non-randomised study at five centres, 44 patients received SonoClear and 40 contributed to paired comparisons with standard irrigation fluid. SonoClear reduced below-cavity artefactual signal (ratio of contrast-to-noise ratios, irrigation/SonoClear: 1.70; 95% CI, 1.48–1.95). Five independent neurosurgeons masked to the fluid reported a mean paired Surgeon Image Rating improvement of 1.96 points (95% CI, 1.80–2.11). No serious adverse events were judged probably or definitely device-related within 30 days; postoperative magnetic resonance imaging showed no major findings in 36 evaluated patients. These findings support acoustic matching to improve ultrasound guidance, including at resection completion; effects on resection extent and patient outcomes require investigation.

title: Epilepsy as an Initial Presentation of Superficial Siderosis of the Central Nervous System:A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background Superficial siderosis of the central nervous system (SSCNS) is a rare neurological disorder resulting from chronic subarachnoid haemorrhage. Its classical clinical features comprise sensorineural hearing loss, cerebellar ataxia and pyramidal tract dysfunction. However, epilepsy as an initial presentation remains uncommon and insufficiently characterized. Case Presentation: We describe a 34-year-old male with a remote history of right brachial plexus injury, who presented with recurrent epileptic seizures as the predominant early symptom, followed by progressive hearing loss and gait instability. Neuroimaging demonstrated characteristic haemosiderin deposition on T2*-weighted and susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI) sequences.Transient, seizure-related subcortical and periventricular restricted diffusion on diffusion-weighted imaging resolved completely within one month. Anti-epileptic medication achieved partial seizure control, but the patient’s neurological deficits exhibited gradual progression. Conclusion Epilepsy may represent an uncommon initial presentation of SSCNS. Targeted MRI sequences facilitate diagnosis. SSCNS should be considered in the differential diagnosis of patients with unexplained epilepsy,particularly those with a history of craniospinal trauma.

title: A Dynamic, Intraoperative-Triggered Strategy for Early Bilateral Uterine Artery Ligation During Cesarean Myomectomy in Pregnancies with Giant Fibroids in High-Risk Locations: A Retrospective Case Series of Ten Patients
abstract: Abstract Background Pregnancy complicated by giant uterine fibroids in high-risk locations (retroplacental, cervical, submucosal, or intraligamentary) carries a risk of serious obstetric hemorrhage during cesarean myomectomy (CM). Current practice lacks a standardized intraoperative hemostatic decision strategy; most approaches rely on a static preoperative risk label that cannot fully accommodate the dynamic reality of surgical bleeding. Methods We retrospectively analyzed a prospectively implemented institutional protocol at a tertiary referral center in Beijing, China (January 2022–November 2025). Ten consecutive patients with singleton pregnancies and at least one giant fibroid (≥ 8 cm) in a high-risk location were managed under a dynamic dual-decision framework: (1) preoperative magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based multidisciplinary team (MDT) risk stratification guided surgical preparedness; and (2) the decision to perform early bilateral uterine artery ligation (BUAL) was made intraoperatively, at the first recognition that bleeding was active and accelerating — before progression to established hemorrhage. The bleeding rate that triggered this clinical judgment was calibrated retrospectively against a 150 mL/min threshold, a recognized criterion for massive hemorrhage. The primary outcome was estimated blood loss (EBL). The STROBE guideline was followed. Results Ten patients were included (mean age 36.5 years; mean fibroid diameter 12.8 cm). Three patients (Cases 2, 5, and 6; mean diameter 17.7 cm) met the intraoperative trigger and received early BUAL, yielding a mean EBL of 343 mL (range 200–600 mL). The remaining seven patients were managed without BUAL: four with tailored location-specific techniques at intrapartum cesarean, one with antepartum laparoscopic myomectomy, one with postpartum transvaginal resection, and one with expectant management. The overall mean EBL was 256.5 mL. No patient required blood transfusion. Conclusions This preliminary case series describes an intraoperative-triggered strategy for early BUAL during CM in pregnancies with high-risk giant fibroids. The approach is hypothesis-generating rather than definitive evidence of efficacy or safety; larger prospective studies with control groups are required. Within the limits of a small, single-center, retrospective case series without a control group, the strategy was associated with modest blood loss and no transfusion, and may be of particular relevance in settings where blood transfusion is not reliably available.

Three patients (Cases 2, 5, and 6; mean diameter 17.7 cm) met the intraoperative trigger and received early BUAL, yielding a mean EBL of 343 mL (range 200–600 mL). The remaining seven patients were managed without BUAL: four with tailored location-specific techniques at intrapartum cesarean, one with antepartum laparoscopic myomectomy, one with postpartum transvaginal resection, and one with expectant management. The overall mean EBL was 256.5 mL. No patient required blood transfusion. Conclusions This preliminary case series describes an intraoperative-triggered strategy for early BUAL during CM in pregnancies with high-risk giant fibroids. The approach is hypothesis-generating rather than definitive evidence of efficacy or safety; larger prospective studies with control groups are required. Within the limits of a small, single-center, retrospective case series without a control group, the strategy was associated with modest blood loss and no transfusion, and may be of particular relevance in settings where blood transfusion is not reliably available.

title: A modified ¹⁸F-FDG PET/CT diagnostic criterion for regional lymph node metastasis in gastric cancer: a multicenter retrospective study
abstract: Abstract Background Lymph‑node metastasis represents the dominant metastatic pathway and a critical prognostic factor for gastric cancer. Therefore, accurate pre‑treatment evaluation of regional lymph nodes is clinically essential. Nevertheless, preoperative ¹⁸F‑FDG PET/CT exhibits limited diagnostic performance in routine practice. This study hypothesized that such limitation partially originates from drawbacks of conventional diagnostic criteria, and proposed a modified hierarchical criterion combining metabolic and morphological features to improve PET/CT diagnostic performance for lymph‑node metastasis. Methods Of 173 patients with histologically confirmed gastric adenocarcinoma initially enrolled from three tertiary hospitals, 166 patients with 507 evaluable lymph node groups were included in the final retrospective analysis. Analyses were performed at the lymph‑node group level to account for within‑patient clustering. Two diagnostic criteria were compared: Criterion 1 (conventional, purely SUVmax‑based metabolic criterion) and Criterion 2 (modified hierarchical criterion integrating metabolic and contrast‑enhanced CT morphological features). Diagnostic performance metrics including area under the receiver‑operating‑characteristic curve (AUC), accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), and negative predictive value (NPV) were calculated. Performance was further stratified by lymph‑node groups and pathological subtypes. Results Compared with Criterion 1, Criterion 2 yielded significantly improved diagnostic performance for lymph‑node metastasis (AUC: 79.80% vs. 62.70%; accuracy: 84.02% vs. 56.41%; sensitivity: 90.79% vs 47.62%; specificity: 69.59% vs 80.05%; PPV: 83.83% vs 78.30%; NPV: 78.67% vs 49.79%; DeLong test, P < 0.01). Subgroup analyses demonstrated superior performance of Criterion 2 across all Lauren subtypes ( P < 0.05). For WHO pathological subtypes, Criterion 2 achieved higher AUC values relative to Criterion 1; the difference reached marginal statistical significance for tubular adenocarcinoma (TAC, adjusted DeLong test, P = 0.053), whereas statistically significant differences were observed for the remaining subtypes (DeLong test, P < 0.05). Regarding individual lymph‑node group, Criterion 2 showed improved diagnostic efficiency for stations 1, 3A, 4SA, 7, 8, and 9 (DeLong test, P < 0.05). Conclusions The diagnostic performance of ¹⁸F‑FDG PET/CT for regional gastric‑cancer lymph‑node metastasis is strongly dependent on the applied diagnostic criteria. The proposed modified hierarchical criterion integrating metabolic and morphological features outperforms the conventional purely metabolic criterion and shows potential for preoperative clinical application.

title: Automated vs. Traditional Reconstruction Workflows for Head and Neck CTA: Effects on Exam Duration and Variability
abstract: Abstract Background and Purpose Rapid and reliable stroke imaging is critical for timely diagnosis and intervention. Traditional workflows for head and neck CT angiography (CTA) involve manual image reconstruction steps that can prolong exam completion times and increase variability. This study aimed to evaluate whether an automated, software-driven reconstruction workflow could reduce stroke CTA exam duration and improve efficiency without compromising image quality. Materials and Methods This HIPAA-compliant, retrospective study included 100 consecutive stroke CTA examinations performed on a single emergency department scanner (Siemens SOMATOM Force, Forchheim, Germany) between August and November 2022. Fifty scans were obtained immediately prior to implementation of the automated workflow and 50 scans after a one-month technologist training period post-implementation. Exclusion criteria included repeat imaging due to motion, exams adjacent to other CT angiograms or trauma panscans, and post-intervention cases with technologist adjustments to the automated sequence. All scans were acquired at 100 kVp with intravenous iohexol 350 (50 mL) at 4–5 mL/s, followed by bolus tracking. The primary outcome was total exam completion time; secondary outcomes included technologist active time and variability measures. Results Implementation of the automated workflow resulted in a significant reduction in median exam completion time compared with the traditional workflow. Automated processing decreased median exam time by approximately 8.5 minutes and reduced technologist active time by 14.1 minutes, with narrower standard deviations for both metrics. These improvements were achieved without changes in image acquisition parameters or diagnostic quality. The streamlined process eliminated repetitive manual reconstruction tasks, allowing technologists to focus on patient care and other critical responsibilities. Conclusions Transitioning to an automated reconstruction workflow for stroke CTA substantially improves efficiency by reducing exam duration and technologist workload. In practice settings where radiologists review images after full exam completion, this approach accelerates image availability in PACS, enabling faster detection and communication of critical findings. While immediate clinical impact may vary depending on real-time interpretation practices, earlier availability of reformatted images can facilitate prompt identification of large vessel occlusions and other emergent conditions. Adoption of automated workflows represents a practical strategy to optimize imaging operations amid increasing imaging volumes and technologist shortages.

title: The STABLE Trial: Sustained Breath-Hold During Tissue Acquisition in Robotic Bronchoscopy—A Randomized Controlled Trial
abstract: Abstract Background: Respiratory motion and anesthesia-associated atelectasis may contribute to CT-to-body divergence and reduce the precision of peripheral pulmonary lesion sampling. Breath-hold ventilation has been proposed to stabilize the target and biopsy tool during robotic bronchoscopy, but prospective randomized evidence is limited. We evaluated whether sustained breath-hold during tissue acquisition improves diagnostic yield or tool-lesion positioning during imaging-integrated robotic bronchoscopy. Methods: The STABLE ( S tudy of T ool-lesion A lignment and B reath-hold Ventilation in Robotic Bronchoscopy for Peripheral Lung LE sions) Trial was a prospective randomized study of patients undergoing robotic bronchoscopy for peripheral pulmonary lesions using the Noah Galaxy system with integrated augmented fluoroscopy and C-arm-based tomosynthesis. Patients were randomized to standardized sustained breath-hold during tissue acquisition or conventional ventilation during tissue acquisition; both groups underwent brief breath-holds during AF/CABT image acquisition. The primary endpoint was strict diagnostic yield according to ATS/ACCP definitions, independently adjudicated by a pulmonologist blinded to ventilation assignment. Secondary endpoints included successful lesion localization, tool-in-lesion (TIL), tool-touching-lesion (TTL), no tool in lesion (NTL), radiation exposure, and complications. Standardized mean differences (SMDs) assessed baseline balance. Results: Among 117 randomized patients, 53 underwent breath-hold and 64 conventional ventilation. Mean age was 67.5±10.0 versus 66.3±10.4 years, and mean lesion diameter was 1.7±0.7 versus 1.9±0.8 cm, respectively. Most baseline characteristics were similar; the largest imbalances involved bronchus sign (34.0% vs 51.6%; absolute SMD 0.35) and left-upper-lobe location (28.3% vs 45.3%; SMD 0.35). Overall strict adjudicated diagnostic yield was 89.7% (105/117). Diagnostic yield was 86.8% with breath-hold and 92.2% with conventional ventilation (OR 0.56, 95% CI 0.17–1.87, p-value 0.34). With greater than 1 year of ongoing follow-up, overall diagnostic accuracy was 97.4% (114/117). Nearly all procedures achieved TIL or TTL (98.1% vs 96.9%). TIL occurred in 62.3% versus 64.1% (OR 0.93, 95% CI 0.44–1.97). Localization, tool-position distribution, sampling intensity, radiation exposure, and complications showed no clear between-group differences. Two pneumothoraces requiring chest-tube placement occurred (2/117; 1.7%), both in the conventional ventilation group. Across both groups, diagnostic yield increased from 0% with NTL to 85.0% with TTL and 95.9% with TIL. Conclusions: Sustained breath-hold during tissue acquisition did not improve diagnostic yield or tool-lesion positioning during imaging-integrated robotic bronchoscopy. Diagnostic yield varied according to imaging-confirmed tool-lesion position, supporting procedural strategies that prioritize accurate real-time positioning rather than breath-hold alone. Trial registration: International Standard Randomised Controlled Trial Number (ISRCTN) Registry, ISRCTN11802169; retrospectively registered (01/09/2026).

title: Prognostic Analysis of Iodine-avid Residual Metastatic Lymph Nodes in Differentiated Thyroid Cancer
abstract: Abstract Backgroud : In clinical practice, even with equivalent administered radioiodine( 131 I) activities, metastatic lymph node lesions exhibit heterogeneous responses to initial 131 I therapy among differentiated thyroid cancer (DTC )patients. Objectives To evaluate the efficacy of initial 131 I treatment in DTC patients with iodine-avid residual metastatic lymph nodes (reLNs) and to develop a model for predicting the functional 131 I therapy response. Methods 220 DTC patients who underwent initial 131 I therapy with iodine-avid reLNs on Rx-WBS (post-therapy whole-body scan with SPECT/CT) were included retrospectively in this study. Imaging features of reLNs, including number, maximum short-axis diameter, calcification, and semiquantitative 131 I uptake indices, together with pre-therapy stimulated thyroglobulin (ps-Tg) and administrated 131 I activity were analyzed. 131 I therapy response was assessed according to the 2015 American Thyroid Association criteria. Functional 131 I therapy response was defined as two groups by disappearance or persistence of iodine uptake on reLNs according to the follow-up scans. To predict the functional 131 I therapy response, logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors and a nomogram was constructed and validated. Results After initial 131 I therapy, patients exhibited excellent response (ER, 44.5%), indeterminate response (IDR, 30.0%), biochemically incomplete response (IR, 11.4%), and structurally incomplete response (SIR,14.1%), respectively. In terms of functional outcomes, 86.8% of patients had complete resolution of radioactive iodine uptake, while persistent iodine uptake was observed in the remaining 13.2% of cases. Compared with the disappearance group, the persistent 131 I uptake group had higher administrated 131 I activity, higher ps-Tg levels, more iodine-avid lymph nodes, larger maximum short-axis diameter and more frequent calcification of the reLNs. Multivariable analysis identified ps-Tg and number of iodine-avid reLNs as independent risk factors for 131 I persistent uptake. In the imaging-only model, lymph node number and maximum short-axis diameter were positively associated with 131 I persistent uptake. The nomogram achieved an AUC of 0.792 (95% CI, 0.678–0.906). Conclusion Initial 131 I therapy yielded favorable outcomes in DTC patients with iodine-avid reLNs. The number and size of reLNs serve as key predictors of persistent radioactive iodine uptake. A novel nomogram incorporating ps-Tg, metastatic nodal number, and maximum short-axis diameter was constructed to preliminarily achieve individualized prediction of functional therapeutic response.

title: Atypical Sturge–Weber syndrome Type III without facial nevus presenting as acute focal neurological deficit in a child: a case report
abstract: Abstract We report the case of a 4-year-old female who presented with high-grade fever and acute left-sided weakness. Initial non-contrast CT suggested acute encephalitis, leading to a provisional diagnosis of partially treated meningoencephalitis and illustrating the potential for diagnostic misinterpretation. However, contrast-enhanced MRI revealed leptomeningeal enhancement, cortical atrophy, and dilated deep medullary veins, consistent with atypical Sturge–Weber syndrome Type III. The patient improved with supportive management. This case highlights the diagnostic challenge of atypical SWS and underscores the crucial role of contrast-enhanced MRI when CT findings are nonspecific or misleading.

title: Prognostic Value of Baseline ¹⁸F-FDG PET/CT Metabolic Tumor Burden in Multiple Myeloma
abstract: Abstract Purpose To evaluate prognostic value of baseline ¹⁸F-FDG PET/CT Metabolic tumor burden in multiple myeloma. Methods This retrospective, single-center study included 148 patients with newly diagnosed MM who underwent baseline ¹⁸F-FDG PET/CT before systemic therapy. Total metabolic tumor volume (tMTV), total lesion glycolysis (TLG), SUVmax, and morphologic findings were evaluated. Overall survival was analyzed using Kaplan–Meier methods and Cox regression; receiver operating characteristic analyses (ROC) assessed discrimination for mortality. Results Median tMTV, TLG, and SUVmax were 92.55, 272, and 5.2, respectively. Paramedullary and extramedullary disease were present in 37.8% and 11.5% of patients. During a median follow-up of 319 days, 41 patients (27.7%) died. TLG had the highest discrimination for mortality (area under the curve, 0.674), whereas tMTV was the only independent imaging predictor of overall survival among imaging variables (hazard ratio, 1.07 per 100-unit increase; P = .01). The exploratory optimal tMTV threshold was > 288. Conclusion Baseline ¹⁸F-FDG PET/CT-derived volumetric measures provide prognostic information in newly diagnosed MM. tMTV may complement conventional risk assessment, but the proposed threshold requires external validation.

title: First Adult Case of Echovirus 21–Associated Poliomyelitis-Like Myelitis Presenting with Flaccid Asymmetric Tetraparesis
abstract: Abstract Background Non-polio enterovirus–associated myelitis is a rare condition causing acute flaccid paralysis due to anterior horn cell injury. While most cases occur in children, reports in adults are exceedingly uncommon. Methods We report the first known case in a 63-year-old woman with relapsed/refractory mantle cell lymphoma (MCL) after second-line therapy with rituximab and ibrutinib. Following leukapheresis for planned CAR-T-cell therapy, she received bridging chemotherapy with bendamustine, cytarabine, and rituximab. During prolonged neutropenia and lymphopenia, she developed sudden asymmetric tetraparesis. Diagnostic workup included brain and spinal MRI, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis with cytology and flow cytometry, nerve conduction studies (NCS), and electromyography (EMG). Results NCS and EMG demonstrated a predominantly axonal neuropathy with acute denervation. Spinal MRI revealed cervical intramedullary T2 hyperintensities with a characteristic “snake-eye” sign involving the anterior horns. CSF analysis showed normal cell counts and protein levels without lymphoma involvement. Multiplex PCR detected enteroviruses, subsequently identified as Echovirus-21. Initial treatment with intravenous immunoglobulins for suspected Guillain–Barré syndrome was discontinued after confirmation of enterovirus-associated myelitis, and supportive care was provided. Discussion Although rare in adults, enterovirus-associated myelitis should be considered in immunosuppressed patients presenting with acute flaccid paralysis. Early diagnosis using spinal MRI, CSF PCR, and electrodiagnostic studies is essential to avoid misdiagnosis and inappropriate treatment.

title: Single-port inflatable video-assisted mediastinoscopic transhiatal esophagectomy for esophageal cancer in a patient with left upper lobe destruction secondary to remote pulmonary tuberculosis: a case report
abstract: Abstract Background Surgical resection is the cornerstone of curative treatment for resectable esophageal cancer. However, transthoracic esophagectomy (TTE) requires one-lung ventilation (OLV), which may be poorly tolerated by patients with severely impaired pulmonary function. Inflatable video-assisted mediastinoscopic transhiatal esophagectomy combined with laparoscopy (IVMTE), which avoids OLV, may offer an alternative surgical approach for these patients. Case presentation A 70-year-old man presented with a 1-month history of dysphagia. Endoscopic biopsy confirmed mid-thoracic esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). He had a history of pulmonary tuberculosis with radiographic evidence of left upper lobe destruction. Pulmonary function testing revealed severe restrictive ventilatory impairment with impaired diffusing capacity, rendering him unable to tolerate transthoracic surgery. Following multidisciplinary evaluation, he underwent single-port inflatable video-assisted mediastinoscopic transhiatal esophagectomy combined with laparoscopy (SP-IVMTE), with an uneventful intraoperative course and no oxygen desaturation. Histopathology revealed a moderately differentiated squamous cell carcinoma invading the adventitia, with negative margins and no lymph node metastasis (pT3N0M0). The patient had an uneventful postoperative recovery and was discharged on postoperative day 14. The patient had an uneventful postoperative recovery. Follow-up CT scans through 24 months showed no evidence of recurrence or metastasis, and at the 29-month clinical follow-up, he remained asymptomatic with normal oral intake. Conclusions For patients with severely compromised pulmonary reserve who are unable to tolerate a transthoracic approach, IVMTE may provide a feasible individualized surgical option for curative treatment of esophageal cancer.

title: Diagnostic and Perioperative Complexity when Retroperitoneal Hemangioma Mimics Sympathetic Paraganglioma: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background. Primary retroperitoneal tumors, which comprise 0.1–0.2% of all malignancies, can encompass various etiologies, and possess nonspecific imaging features. These factors make them a diagnosis of exclusion, especially in adult patients. Additionally, fewer than 50 cases of adult primary cavernous hemangiomas in the retroperitoneal space have been reported. However, when a hypervascular retroperitoneal mass is accompanied by hypertension and ambivalent serum catecholamine levels, a functional sympathetic paraganglioma becomes the leading diagnosis as it requires a differential work up, driving a high-stakes perioperative pathway. Case Presentation. A 52-year-old man with insulin dependent type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, hyperlipidemia and schizoaffective disorder had a well vascularized retroperitoneal mass incidentally identified on trauma imaging following a motor vehicular accident (MVA). Cross-sectional imaging and mildly-to-moderately elevated urinary and plasma catecholamines/Metanephrines raised concern for a functional paraganglioma. He underwent preoperative alpha then beta-adrenergic blockade and laparoscopic resection. Final Histopathology demonstrated a cavernous hemangioma with no neuroendocrine tissue. Conclusions. The combination of chronic hypertension, anxiety, and equivocal biochemistry produced a convincing phenotype for functional paraganglioma. Since unprepared resection of a functional paraganglioma carries substantial perioperative cardiovascular risk, alpha-blockade optimization was justified even though the lesion proved non-functional. Poorly controlled diabetes with marked perioperative glycemic variability added independent surgical risk. Since hypervascular retroperitoneal masses are rare in adults; if the diagnosis of a functional paraganglioma cannot be excluded, the safest course is to prepare as though the mass were one.

title: Comparison of two- and three-dimensional computed tomography-based deep-learning models with neurosurgeon assessments for predicting functional outcome at discharge in patients with spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage: a single-center retrospective study
abstract: Abstract Background Early prediction of short-term functional outcome after spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage (sICH) remains challenging. Non-contrast computed tomography (NCCT) provides essential imaging information, whereas the Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) reflects early neurological severity. This study evaluated whether two-dimensional (2D) slice-based and three-dimensional (3D) volume-based deep-learning models integrating NCCT and clinical information could predict short-term functional outcome in patients with sICH and compared their performance with neurosurgeon assessments. Methods This single-center retrospective study included 286 patients with sICH who underwent NCCT within 24 h after hemorrhage onset. Functional outcome at discharge was dichotomized according to the Glasgow Outcome Scale. Patients were divided into training and testing cohorts. A 2D model was trained using hemorrhage-containing NCCT slices (without manual voxel-wise segmentation), with patient-level prediction obtained through majority voting. A 3D model was trained using whole-brain CT volumes combined with clinical information. Three neurosurgeons independently predicted outcomes. Model performance was evaluated using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and area under the curve (AUC). Results The 2D image-only baseline model achieved 81.0% accuracy (AUC = 0.812). Incorporating admission GCS improved the 2D model performance to 90.3% accuracy (AUC = 0.903). The 3D model achieved 90.6% accuracy (AUC = 0.895). Both deep-learning models showed higher accuracy in short-term outcome prediction than did neurosurgeon assessments. No significant difference was observed between the best-performing 2D and 3D models. Conclusion NCCT-based deep-learning models incorporating admission GCS may improve short-term outcome prediction after sICH. The 2D model achieved performance comparable to that of the 3D model, required less clinical information, and showed higher predictive efficiency. Prospective multicenter validation is required.

title: The Application of Video‑Electroencephalographic Monitoring Combined with Multimodal Imaging in Surgical Management of Secondary Epilepsy in Children
abstract: Abstract Objective To explore the clinical value of video‑electroencephalography (VEEG) coupled with multimodal imaging for pre‑surgical epileptogenic‑zone localization, surgical planning and prognostic evaluation in children with drug‑resistant epilepsy. Methods : A retrospective analysis was performed on 42 pediatric patients who underwent epilepsy surgery. Pre‑operative workup included brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), long‑term scalp VEEG, and PET‑CT for selected participants. For diagnostically challenging cases, stereoelectroencephalography (SEEG) depth electrodes or electrocorticography (ECoG) cortical electrodes were implanted to refine epileptogenic‑zone identification. Cortical electrical stimulation (CES) and somatosensory evoked potentials (SEP) were applied to map eloquent brain regions. Intra‑operative cortical electrophysiological monitoring guided lesion resection. Individualized surgical strategies were adopted according to lesion characteristics. Post‑operative follow‑up spanned 1‑4 years, and seizure outcomes were assessed using the modified Engel classification. Results : ① Pre‑operative brain MRI revealed heterogeneous epileptogenic etiologies, most frequently temporal‑lobe signal abnormalities (17 cases) and focal cortical developmental anomalies (12 cases). ② Long‑term VEEG allowed detailed recording of background electroencephalographic rhythms; sleep markedly elevated the yield of interictal epileptiform discharges. Interictal discharges were captured in 35 patients, and spontaneous clinical seizure discharges were successfully recorded in 15 patients. ③ Among 21 patients receiving PET‑CT, focal hypometabolism was observed within most lesion territories. ④ Combined long‑term VEEG with intracranial SEEG/ECoG electrodes precisely delineated discharge onset zones, while functional‑mapping techniques ensured operative safety. ⑤ Ten distinct individualized surgical protocols were implemented tailored to underlying pathology. Intra‑operative ECoG detected sharp‑wave activity in 35 patients, informing the extent of surgical resection. ⑥ Integrating MRI findings with post‑surgical histopathology clarified the etiological diagnosis for all patients. ⑦ After 1‑4 years of follow‑up, 33 patients attained Engel class I outcomes, indicating satisfactory overall seizure control. Note: Developmental anomalies encompass structural malformations and signal alterations, collectively termed cortical developmental abnormalities herein. Conclusions :Video‑electroencephalography combined with multimodal imaging including MRI and PET‑CT enables reasonably accurate (though not absolute) dual anatomical‑electrophysiological localization of epileptogenic zones. This multimodal framework provides robust evidence for individualized surgical planning and bears considerable clinical utility.

title: Structured Modality Dropout for Robust MRI-Based IDH Mutation Classification in Glioma
abstract: Abstract The classification of IDH gene mutation is an essential marker in the treatment of a group of brain tumors called glioma, indicating the favorability of prognosis and response to treatment. Current methods determine the IDH mutation status invasively through postoperative tissue and DNA analysis. It is favorable to predict the mutation status non-invasively from MRI scans to determine suitable surgical strategies. Existing MRI-based prediction models often assume the availability of all four MRI modalities. However, in real-world clinical settings, one or more modalities may be missing due to reasons such as image quality and inconsistent protocols. This severely impacts the performance of MRI-based deep learning models. This study proposes a structured modality dropout training strategy to improve the robustness of a 3D ResNet18 model for IDH prediction. We compared three training strategies: Baseline (no dropout), Dropout-30 (moderate), and Dropout-50 (aggressive). All three models were evaluated using five-fold stratified cross-validation across six realistic modality availability scenarios (all four, missing T1CE, missing FLAIR, missing T2, T1 and T2 only, T1 only). Performance was evaluated using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC), balanced accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, Brier score, and bootstrap confidence intervals (CI). Key Findings: The Baseline model performed best when all four modalities were available (AUC $0.823 \pm 0.042$), but the Dropout models showed more stable performance as the number of missing modalities increased. The Dropout-30 model showed the best calibration, with the lowest Brier score of $0.198$. Overall, Dropout-30 was the most balanced and clinically viable model, remaining the most stable across scenarios, best calibrated, and showing good generalization across scanner models.

title: Methodology of a prospective, single-arm, multicenter, physician-initiated study to assess the long-term safety and efficacy of the Restorer stent system for the treatment of aorto-iliac lesions. BARISTA trial.
abstract: Abstract Background Evidence regarding optimal stent selection in endovascular treatment of aorto-iliac lesions remains inconclusive, particularly in complex TASC C and D disease. Interpretation of existing data is complicated by study heterogeneity and selection bias. Both bare metal stents (BMS) and covered stents (CS) are widely used, yet comparative evidence remains limited. The BARISTA trial aims to prospectively evaluate the safety and efficacy of the Restorer iliac stent system (iVascular) and to compare its outcomes with those reported in contemporary studies assessing covered stents. Methods Between July 2022 and June 2024, this prospective multicenter study enrolled 200 patients across 14 Belgian centers. The objective is to assess two-year safety and efficacy outcomes of the Restorer iliac stent system in symptomatic aorto-iliac disease. The primary composite endpoint includes: (1) freedom from target lesion revascularization (TLR), (2) freedom from major amputation, and (3) absence of restenosis within 12 months. TLR is defined as any repeat intervention within the treated segment, including 5 mm proximal and distal to the lesion. Restenosis is defined as > 50% stenosis on duplex ultrasound with a systolic velocity ratio > 2.4. Discussion By analyzing outcomes in a large prospective cohort and comparing results with contemporary CS data, the BARISTA trial aims to support evidence-based stent selection in aorto-iliac disease. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov ID: NCT05293002 (2022-03-23)

title: Predictive Value of Quantitative T2-Weighted MRI Morphometric Parameters for Clinically Significant Prostate Cancer in PI-RADS v2.1 ≥4 Lesions
abstract: Abstract Objective To evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of quantitative T2-weighted MRI morphometric parameters for detecting clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa) in prostate lesions with PI-RADS v2.1 category ≥ 4. Methods This retrospective study included 153 patients who underwent multiparametric MRI according to the PI-RADS v2.1 protocol followed by prostate biopsy. A total of 165 prostate lesions with PI-RADS v2.1 scores ≥4were analyzed. Based on histopathological results, lesions were classified as csPCa or benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH). Quantitative morphometric parameters, including maximum diameter, mean diameter, cross-sectional area, and volume, were measured on tri-planar T2-weighted images. Differences between csPCa and BPH lesions, as well as zone-specific characteristics in the peripheral zone (PZ) and transition zone (TZ), were assessed. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was performed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of each parameter and to determine optimal cutoff values. Results Among the 165 lesions, 108 were csPCa (69 in the PZ and 39 in the TZ) and 57 were BPH (20 in the PZ and 37 in the TZ). csPCa lesions demonstrated significantly larger maximum diameter, mean diameter, area, and volume compared with BPH lesions in both the PZ and TZ (all p < 0.05). ROC analysis showed that lesion volume achieved the highest diagnostic performance among all morphometric parameters, with area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.819 in the PZ and 0.811 in the TZ. The optimal volume thresholds for differentiating csPCa from BPH were 1.23 cm³ in the PZ and 1.07 cm³ in the TZ, respectively. Conclusions In prostate lesions with PI-RADS v2.1 category ≥ 4, lesion volume demonstrates superior diagnostic accuracy compared with maximum diameter, mean diameter, and area. Volume-based assessment may serve as a valuable quantitative imaging biomarker to improve the detection of clinically significant prostate cancer, particularly when accounting for zone-specific differences.

title: Longitudinal MRI Response Phenotypes and Lesion-Level Local Control after Gamma Knife Radiosurgery for Breast Cancer Brain Metastases
abstract: Abstract Purpose Serial magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) demonstrates heterogeneous lesion evolution after stereotactic radiosurgery. We characterized longitudinal volumetric response phenotypes after Gamma Knife radiosurgery (GKRS) for breast cancer brain metastases and examined their association with 12-month lesion-level local control. Methods This single-center retrospective study included 80 patients, 182 GKRS-treated lesions, and 819 serial MRI records. Local control was assessed within a prespecified 10–14-month window. Lesions were classified as complete response/disappearance, partial regression, stable control, or progression. Baseline correlates of local failure were evaluated using Bayesian mixed-effects logistic regression, with patient-clustered generalized estimating equations used for sensitivity analysis. Results Local control was evaluable in 103 lesions and longitudinal phenotype in 154. The four phenotypes comprised 24 complete responses/disappearances, 59 partial regressions, 44 stable controls, and 27 progressions. In the prespecified Bayesian model, larger baseline whole-tumor volume and peritumoral edema were associated with higher odds of local failure, whereas higher BED₁₀ was inversely associated; clustered sensitivity estimates retained the same directions but were less precise. Progression phenotype was strongly associated with local failure after accounting for within-patient clustering (odds ratio 27.08, 95% confidence interval 7.11–103.20; p < 0.001) and remained associated when classification was restricted to the 10–14-month window. Conclusion Longitudinal volumetric MRI phenotypes capture heterogeneous post-GKRS lesion evolution and identify a progression pattern closely associated with local failure. This framework may complement standard local-control assessment during post-treatment surveillance.

title: PathVista Integrates Cellular Foundation Models with Multiscale Histopathology for Colorectal Cancer Prognosis and Molecular Stratification
abstract: Abstract Personalized management of colorectal cancer (CRC) requires accurate risk stratification and identification of clinically actionable molecular alterations. However, standard clinicopathologic features often fail to capture the cellular and tumor microenvironmental heterogeneity driving disease behavior. Although routine hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) whole-slide images (WSIs) reflect these patterns, patch-level foundation models may obscure fine-grained cellular morphology and spatial organization. We present PathVista , a cell-centered framework that integrates cellular and tissue-level representations for prognostic and molecular stratification. PathVista incorporates CellSwAV , a cellular foundation model pretrained on more than 160 million CRC cells and combines spatially aggregated cellular features with broader tissue context. Across 2,568 CRC patients , PathVista risk scores were significantly associated with overall survival (HR = 6.65, 95% CI: 3.53–12.51) , disease-free survival (HR = 3.15, 95% CI: 1.82–5.45) , and recurrence-free survival (HR = 3.04, 95% CI: 1.76–5.26) , with risk scores remaining independently associated with outcomes after clinicopathologic adjustment. Locked models also generalized to external TCGA (HR = 5.25, 95% CI: 2.29–12.05) and SURGEN (HR = 2.89, 95% CI: 1.86–4.49) cohorts. PathVista predicted microsatellite instability (AUC = 0.91) and BRAF mutation status (AUC = 0.83) . Across 4,667 patients spanning CRC, lung, and breast cancers, PathVista demonstrated the potential of cell-centered histopathology for prognostic, molecular, and tumor characterization.

title: A Nerve Root-Centered Classification System for Lumbar Disc Herniation: Development and Reliability Assessment
abstract: Abstract Background Existing classifications of lumbar disc herniation (LDH) mainly describe disc morphology, migration, or canal compromise, but provide limited information regarding the spatial relationship between the herniated disc and the affected nerve root. This study developed a nerve root-centered classification for patients undergoing percutaneous endoscopic lumbar discectomy (PELD) and evaluated its observer reliability and agreement with intraoperative findings. Methods This single-center retrospective classification-development and reliability study included 516 patients with LDH who underwent PELD between January and December 2022. The Peking University Third Hospital (PUTH) classification integrates the cranio-caudal origin pattern of the affected nerve root (Types 1–3) with the location of the herniated disc relative to the nerve root (Types A–D). Preliminary classifications based on preoperative magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) were compared with consensus reference classifications established through blinded review of intraoperative videos by senior spine surgeons. Intraobserver and interobserver reliability were evaluated by three surgeons from the study institution using all 516 cases and by five surgeons from external institutions using 100 proportionately stratified cases from the same cohort. Clinical outcomes were summarized descriptively after a minimum follow-up of 2 years. Results MRI-based classifications agreed with the consensus video-based reference classifications in 486 of 516 cases (94.2%). Thirty discordant cases were mainly attributable to severe nerve root compression, incomplete visualization of the nerve root origin on MRI, or anatomical variation. Internal intraobserver agreement was substantial to excellent (κ = 0.776–0.842), and internal interobserver agreement was excellent (κ = 0.837). Among external raters, intraobserver agreement was substantial (κ = 0.659–0.756), whereas interobserver agreement was also substantial but lower than that observed internally (κ = 0.645). At final follow-up, lower VAS and ODI scores and a higher JOA score were observed compared with preoperative values. Symptomatic recurrence occurred in 13 patients (2.52%), and postoperative complications occurred in 9 patients (1.74%). Conclusion The PUTH classification demonstrated substantial-to-excellent observer reliability and high MRI–operative agreement in a single-center cohort undergoing PELD. Independent prospective multicenter studies are required to determine its generalizability and influence on surgical decision-making and clinical outcomes.

Intraobserver and interobserver reliability were evaluated by three surgeons from the study institution using all 516 cases and by five surgeons from external institutions using 100 proportionately stratified cases from the same cohort. Clinical outcomes were summarized descriptively after a minimum follow-up of 2 years. Results MRI-based classifications agreed with the consensus video-based reference classifications in 486 of 516 cases (94.2%). Thirty discordant cases were mainly attributable to severe nerve root compression, incomplete visualization of the nerve root origin on MRI, or anatomical variation. Internal intraobserver agreement was substantial to excellent (κ = 0.776–0.842), and internal interobserver agreement was excellent (κ = 0.837). Among external raters, intraobserver agreement was substantial (κ = 0.659–0.756), whereas interobserver agreement was also substantial but lower than that observed internally (κ = 0.645). At final follow-up, lower VAS and ODI scores and a higher JOA score were observed compared with preoperative values. Symptomatic recurrence occurred in 13 patients (2.52%), and postoperative complications occurred in 9 patients (1.74%). Conclusion The PUTH classification demonstrated substantial-to-excellent observer reliability and high MRI–operative agreement in a single-center cohort undergoing PELD. Independent prospective multicenter studies are required to determine its generalizability and influence on surgical decision-making and clinical outcomes.

title: Interpretable Concept-Bottleneck Vision-Language Model Predicts Pathologic Complete Response From Longitudinal Breast DCE-MRI
abstract: Abstract Deep learning can predict neoadjuvant treatment response in breast cancer, but most models are black boxes whose reasoning clinicians cannot verify, limiting adoption. We developed an interpretable concept-bottleneck vision-language model (CB-VLM) that predicts pathologic complete response (pCR) from pre-treatment and early-treatment dynamic contrast-enhanced (DCE) MRI, routing every prediction through eleven radiologist-recognizable, BI-RADS-style imaging concepts plus age and molecular subtype. Trained on 753 patients from the multicenter I-SPY2 trial, the model achieved an AUROC of 0.76 on encoder-held-out data (n = 144) and generalized to an independent I-SPY1 cohort (AUC 0.71; n = 110). Accuracy rose with model confidence (88% versus 58% on borderline predictions), and early change in functional tumor volume was the dominant predictor across both cohorts. To our knowledge, this is the first large vision-language model to generate concept-grounded reasoning for breast DCE-MRI treatment response prediction, reframing a black-box task as transparent, auditable, and generalizable.

title: Development and validation of a three-marker urine DNA methylation assay complementary to mpMRI for pre-biopsy risk stratification of clinically significant prostate cancer
abstract: Abstract Background Current prostate cancer (PCa) diagnostic strategies remain limited in accurately identifying clinically significant disease while avoiding unnecessary biopsy. This study aimed to develop and independently validate a non-invasive urine DNA methylation assay using naturally voided, non-digital rectal examination (non-DRE) urine and assess its complementary value with multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI) for detecting clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa; Grade Group ≥ 2). Methods The biomarker discovery phase was initiated using microarray-based DNA methylation profiling to screen for tumor-specific alterations, and the candidate regions were subsequently validated by bisulfite-pyrosequencing in the same tissue specimens. Three prioritized markers– CDYL , EMX2 , and LRRC4– were incorporated into a linear target enrichment quantitative methylation-specific PCR assay. Marker-specific thresholds optimized in a training cohort (n = 33) were locked and evaluated in an independent validation cohort of men undergoing biopsy for suspected PCa (n = 97). All participants underwent pre-biopsy mpMRI and standard prostate biopsy. Of the 97 validation patients, 89 were evaluable for combined-modality analysis, while 8 were excluded due to missing mpMRI scans. Results In the training cohort, the assay achieved 100% sensitivity and 31.6% specificity for csPCa. In the independent validation cohort, standalone assay performance yielded 75.9% sensitivity and 44.2% specificity. Among the 89 patients evaluable for both modalities (49 csPCa, 40 no-csPCa), mpMRI alone (PI-RADS ≥ 4) showed a sensitivity of 69.4%. Combining the urine assay and mpMRI using an either-positive strategy significantly increased diagnostic sensitivity to 91.8% ( P < 0.01 vs. mpMRI alone), with a negative predictive value of 78.9%. In an exploratory analysis of the indeterminate PI-RADS 3 subgroup, the urine assay correctly identified all 4 biopsy-confirmed cases of csPCa (100% sensitivity). Conclusions The three-marker non-DRE urine DNA methylation assay demonstrates independent diagnostic performance and complementarity to mpMRI. Integrating this molecular assay with anatomical imaging significantly enhances csPCa detection compared with mpMRI alone. These findings support prospective evaluation of predefined, integrated MRI-urine methylation algorithms to refine pre-biopsy risk stratification and optimize biopsy decision-making.

title: Successful emicizumab prophylaxis in treatment-refractory acquired von Willebrand syndrome associated with rheumatoid arthritis
abstract: Abstract Acquired von Willebrand syndrome (AVWS) is a rare bleeding disorder characterized by acquired quantitative or qualitative abnormalities of von Willebrand factor (VWF) and may occur in association with autoimmune disease. Management can be challenging when conventional hemostatic and immunomodulatory therapies fail. We report a 63-year-old man with longstanding rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and no personal or family history of abnormal bleeding who developed life-threatening hemorrhage following dental extractions, resulting in airway obstruction requiring tracheostomy and red blood cell transfusion. Evaluation demonstrated an isolated prolonged activated partial thromboplastin time, markedly reduced factor VIII (FVIII) activity, profoundly decreased VWF antigen and activity, and no detectable FVIII inhibitor. The late onset of bleeding, negative genetic testing, poor VWF recovery following high-dose VWF/FVIII concentrate, and underlying autoimmune disease supported a diagnosis of AVWS. Severe VWF deficiency persisted despite treatment with rituximab, methotrexate, and intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG). Emicizumab was subsequently initiated for prophylactic hemostasis. The patient remained free of spontaneous bleeding despite persistent severe reductions in VWF and FVIII measurements and subsequently underwent upper endoscopy with biopsy and colonoscopy without hemorrhagic complications using adjunctive tranexamic acid. To our knowledge, this represents the first reported case of RA-associated AVWS successfully managed with emicizumab prophylaxis. This case demonstrates sustained clinical hemostasis with emicizumab in treatment-refractory AVWS associated with RA and supports further investigation of FVIII-mimetic therapy as a potential prophylactic strategy when conventional therapies are ineffective.

title: A Study on the Application of Multimodal MRI Deep Learning in the Early Detection of Osteonecrosis of the Femoral Head
abstract: Abstract Objective: Osteonecrosis of the femoral head (ONFH) is a debilitating disorder that frequently leads to hip joint dysfunction. Early and accurate diagnosis is crucial to improving clinical outcomes. This study aimed to develop a magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based detection model using the You Only Look Once (YOLO) deep learning framework for automatic identification of early-stage ONFH, and to systematically evaluate how different MRI modalities affect detection performance and their potential for clinical decision support. Methods: We retrospectively collected MRI data from 253 ONFH patients across two medical centers, including T1-weighted Imaging (T1WI) and T2-weighted Imaging (T2WI) sequences. After standardized preprocessing, the dataset was partitioned into training, validation, and test sets (7:1:2). Two sequential experiments were conducted. Experiment 1 compared six YOLO generations (v3, v5, v8, v10, v11, v13) using single-center T1WI data, with precision (P), recall (R), mean average precision (mAP), and inference speed as primary metrics. Experiment 2 applied the optimal model to single-modality (T1WI or T2WI) and multimodal fused images from both centers, using the same metrics to quantify detection efficacy and validate multicenter robustness. Results: In Experiment 1, YOLO v11 outperformed all other models, achieving a mAP@0.5 of 0.966, a recall of 0.941, and a per-frame inference time of 4.9 ms. In Experiment 2, the multimodal fusion input (T1WI+T2WI) yielded the highest performance across all modalities, with a mAP@0.5 of 0.9637, a recall of 0.9388, and the fastest inference time (3.0 ms), surpassing both T1WI (R=0.9159, 4.9 ms) and T2WI (R=0.9113, 6.0 ms) alone. Conclusion: The proposed YOLO v11 model demonstrates excellent performance in MRI-based ONFH detection, and the multimodal fusion strategy further improves both diagnostic accuracy and computational efficiency. This approach addresses the dual clinical requirements for high precision and real-time processing, offering a practical and objective intelligent tool for early ONFH screening.

title: Neural correlates of cognitive enhancement after probiotic supplementation
abstract: Abstract A previous randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial demonstrated that multistrain probiotic supplementation improved visuospatial cognitive performance in older adults with early cognitive impairment. Participants from a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (N = 68; probiotic, n = 32; placebo, n = 36) underwent T1-weighted magnetic resonance imaging at baseline and after 52 weeks. Cortical surface area and thickness were quantified using FreeSurfer-based surface morphometry. Between-group differences in longitudinal changes were assessed using t-tests and analysis of covariance adjusted for baseline values and demographic covariates. Compared with placebo, the probiotic group showed increased surface area in the left lingual gyrus (+ 21.53 vs. −54.39 mm², p = 3.12 × 10⁻⁴) and cuneus (+ 5.31 vs. −26.28 mm², p = 0.002). Cortical thickness decreased modestly in these regions in the probiotic group. Structural changes in the lingual gyrus and cuneus were associated with visuospatial cognitive performance. Multistrain probiotic supplementation was associated with region-specific longitudinal cortical changes in the left lingual gyrus and cuneus, particularly in cortical surface area. These morphometric changes were associated with visuospatial cognitive performance in older adults with early cognitive impairment.

title: High-Frequency Ultrasound as a Clinical Tool for Diagnosing Pediatric Anterior Talofibular Ligament Injuries and Guiding Conservative Treatment of Avulsion Fractures
abstract: Abstract Background： Pediatric anterior talofibular ligament (ATFL) injuries differ from those in adults, with avulsion injuries occurring frequently at the ligament attachment sites. Small avulsion fractures may be difficult to detect, while objective imaging parameters for treatment planning and follow-up remain limited. This study evaluated the diagnostic and prognostic utility of high-frequency ultrasound (US) in pediatric ATFL injuries. Methods： We retrospectively analyzed 194 pediatric patients with ATFL injuries who underwent high-frequency US between December 2024 and March 2026. Thirty-two surgically treated patients were included in a diagnostic comparison of US and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), using intraoperative findings as the reference standard. Forty-two patients with ATFL avulsion fractures treated conservatively and followed by US for 3 months were included in the prognostic analysis. The sensitivity and specificity of US and MRI for complete ATFL tears and avulsion fractures were assessed. The avulsion fracture separation distance was measured on US, and its ability to predict healing was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. Measurement reproducibility was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs). Results： Among the 194 patients, avulsion fracture was the predominant injury pattern, occurring in 129 (66.5%). In the surgical cohort, complete ATFL tears were confirmed in 6 patients and avulsion fractures in 26. For complete tears, US showed a sensitivity of 83.3% compared with 66.7% for MRI. For avulsion fractures, US demonstrated 100% sensitivity versus 80.8% for MRI, with 100% specificity for both modalities. Among the 42 conservatively treated patients, 25 (59.5%) demonstrated healing at 3 months. Avulsion fracture separation distance showed excellent predictive performance for healing (AUC, 0.935; 95% CI, 0.814–0.988; P < 0.001). A cutoff of ≤0.95 mm yielded 92.0% sensitivity and 82.4% specificity. Interobserver and intraobserver agreement were excellent (ICC, 0.962 and 0.971, respectively). Conclusions： High-frequency US provides sensitive detection of pediatric ATFL avulsion fractures and enables quantitative assessment of avulsion fracture separation. A separation distance of ≤0.95 mm was associated with a higher likelihood of healing after conservative treatment. High-frequency US may therefore provide orthopedists with practical diagnostic and prognostic information to support treatment planning and follow-up in pediatric ATFL injuries.

title: Snowman-like appearance in spinal capillary hemangioma with combined intra- and extramedullary components: two case reports
abstract: Abstract Background Capillary hemangiomas are benign tumors primarily found in the soft tissues of the head and neck, and their occurrence in the spinal cord is rare. Because of its rarity and nonspecific radiological features, it is often difficult to differentiate from more common intradural-extramedullary tumors. Case presentation: We report two cases of thoracic spinal capillary hemangioma with intra- and extramedullary components. MRI demonstrated strongly and homogeneously enhancing tumors with a snowman-like appearance. Intraoperatively, both tumors were highly vascular, with contiguous intra- and extramedullary components closely associated with the spinal pia mater. The tumors were resected en bloc after control of tumor-related vessels. Histopathological examination demonstrated proliferation of capillary-sized vessels without stromal cells, consistent with capillary hemangioma. Postoperative recovery was uneventful. Conclusion A snowman-like appearance is not necessarily specific to spinal hemangioblastoma and may also occur in spinal capillary hemangioma with combined intra- and extramedullary components. Capillary hemangioma should therefore be considered in the differential diagnosis when this imaging pattern is observed.

title: An Efficient and Explainable CNN-Transformer Architecture for Brain Tumor MRI Classification with Deployment-Oriented Benchmarking
abstract: Abstract Brain tumor classification from MRI is essential for treatment planning, but manual interpretation by radiologists is time-consuming and prone to inter-observer variability. Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) capture local texture effectively but have a limited receptive field, whereas Vision Transformers (ViTs) model global context but require large training datasets and lack spatial inductive bias. Existing hybrid CNN-ViT studies on this task, however, rarely benchmark against classical baselines, report computational costs, provide dual visual explainability, or address the risk of patient-level data leakage. The paper proposes a hybrid architecture that sequentially combines a pretrained ResNet50 backbone with a lightweight Transformer Encoder head, converting intermediate CNN feature maps into visual tokens to jointly model fine-grained local lesion detail and global anatomical context. The model is evaluated on the 7200 image datasets (glioma, meningioma, pituitary tumor, no tumor) using stratified 5-fold cross-validation with statistical significance testing, and it is compared to a PCA-SVM baseline built on the same CNN features to isolate the Transformer’s contribution. Computational efficiency (parameters, FLOPS, latency, peak memory) and dual-level explainability (Grad-CAM for the CNN branch, Attention Rollout for the Transformer branch) are also assessed. The proposed model achieves 97.40% ± 0.24% mean cross-validation accuracy, significantly outperforming the PCA-SVM baseline (paired t-test, p = 2.42 x 10^-5) while requiring only 37.20M parameters and 9.21 GFLOPs, an overhead of only 13.68M additional parameters and 0.95 additional GFLOPS (an 11.5% increase) over the CNN-only backbone. These findings position the proposed framework as an accurate, computationally efficient, and interpretable solution for automated brain tumor MRI classification.

title: Development and Validation of a Machine Learning Model for Predicting Pulmonary Embolism Using Routine Clinical Features
abstract: Abstract Background Pulmonary embolism (PE) is a life‑threatening cardiovascular emergency with non‑specific presentations, making timely diagnosis challenging. Over‑reliance on computed tomography pulmonary angiography (CTPA) has raised concerns about radiation exposure and healthcare costs. Traditional clinical prediction rules, such as the Wells and Geneva scores, have limited specificity and fail to capture complex interactions among risk factors. Machine learning (ML) offers a promising alternative, but many existing models lack interpretability or depend on features not routinely available in emergency settings. Objective To develop and internally validate a parsimonious, interpretable ML model for predicting PE using routinely available clinical variables, and to apply SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to enhance model transparency. Methods We conducted a retrospective study of 519 patients suspected of PE at a single tertiary referral center. Eight independent predictors—age, hyperlipidemia, limb circumference, D‑dimer, oxygen saturation, dyspnea, immobility, and malignancy—were identified via univariate and multivariable logistic regression on the training set. Three ML algorithms (Lasso, Random Forest, and XGBoost) were trained and evaluated on a 70/30 train‑test split. Model performance was assessed using AUC‑ROC, calibration plots, and Brier score. SHAP analysis was performed for global and local interpretability. Results On the testing set, Lasso achieved an AUC of 0.766 (95% CI: 0.691–0.840), while XGBoost showed a comparable AUC of 0.764 (95% CI: 0.690–0.837). XGBoost was selected as the primary model due to its superior interpretability via SHAP. At the optimal threshold of 0.526, XGBoost achieved a sensitivity of 74.4%, specificity of 66.7%, and overall accuracy of 71.0%. Calibration was moderate (Brier score = 0.224 vs. null model 0.247; Hosmer‑Lemeshow P = 0.563). SHAP analysis identified limb circumference, D‑dimer, and malignancy as the top three contributors to PE risk. Conclusions The XGBoost model based on eight routine clinical features demonstrated moderate discriminative ability and good interpretability for predicting PE. This tool may serve as a decision‑support aid for emergency physicians in risk stratification, potentially reducing unnecessary CTPA utilization. However, the high PE prevalence (55.6%) in our tertiary cohort limits generalizability; external validation in broader, low‑prevalence populations is essential before clinical implementation. Trial registration : Not applicable (retrospective observational study).

Objective To develop and internally validate a parsimonious, interpretable ML model for predicting PE using routinely available clinical variables, and to apply SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to enhance model transparency. Methods We conducted a retrospective study of 519 patients suspected of PE at a single tertiary referral center. Eight independent predictors—age, hyperlipidemia, limb circumference, D‑dimer, oxygen saturation, dyspnea, immobility, and malignancy—were identified via univariate and multivariable logistic regression on the training set. Three ML algorithms (Lasso, Random Forest, and XGBoost) were trained and evaluated on a 70/30 train‑test split. Model performance was assessed using AUC‑ROC, calibration plots, and Brier score. SHAP analysis was performed for global and local interpretability. Results On the testing set, Lasso achieved an AUC of 0.766 (95% CI: 0.691–0.840), while XGBoost showed a comparable AUC of 0.764 (95% CI: 0.690–0.837). XGBoost was selected as the primary model due to its superior interpretability via SHAP. At the optimal threshold of 0.526, XGBoost achieved a sensitivity of 74.4%, specificity of 66.7%, and overall accuracy of 71.0%. Calibration was moderate (Brier score = 0.224 vs. null model 0.247; Hosmer‑Lemeshow P = 0.563). SHAP analysis identified limb circumference, D‑dimer, and malignancy as the top three contributors to PE risk. Conclusions The XGBoost model based on eight routine clinical features demonstrated moderate discriminative ability and good interpretability for predicting PE. This tool may serve as a decision‑support aid for emergency physicians in risk stratification, potentially reducing unnecessary CTPA utilization. However, the high PE prevalence (55.6%) in our tertiary cohort limits generalizability; external validation in broader, low‑prevalence populations is essential before clinical implementation. title: Investigating renal tissue responses to radiopharmaceutical therapy using multiparametric MRI ​
abstract: Abstract Objectives Renal toxicity is a recognized potential adverse effect of radiopharmaceutical therapy (RPT). While 177 Lu-based therapies are generally well tolerated, subtle therapy-related renal changes remain insufficiently characterized. This study investigated longitudinal renal alterations during 177 Lu-based RPT using multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI) and evaluated its potential for renal monitoring. Methods Twenty-three patients undergoing RPT with either [ 177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE (n = 14) or [ 177 Lu]Lu-PSMA (n = 9) underwent renal mpMRI examinations before and during therapy with up to four treatment cycles. Imaging included arterial spin labeling, diffusion-weighted imaging with intravoxel incoherent motion analysis, blood oxygenation level-dependent imaging, T1 mapping, and volumetry. Renal scintigraphy, estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), and absorbed renal radiation dose were assessed longitudinally. Results No significant decline in eGFR was observed during RPT after exclusion of two patients who developed urinary tract obstruction (p = 0.19). Longitudinal analysis revealed significant temporal changes in T1 values (p = 0.008) and perfusion fraction of IVIM (p = 0.005), as well as a modest decrease in the corticomedullary BOLD ratio (p = 0.020). No significant longitudinal changes were detected for other MRI or scintigraphic parameters. Absorbed renal radiation dose was not associated with changes in MRI-derived biomarkers, eGFR, or renal scintigraphy (all p > 0.05). Patients with urinary obstruction demonstrated distinct MRI abnormalities, including reduced renal blood flow (RBF) and altered BOLD metrics. Conclusions No clinically relevant renal functional deterioration or major imaging abnormalities were detected during contemporary 177 Lu-based RPT. Subtle longitudinal T1 increases may reflect mild structural tissue remodeling without measurable functional consequences. Renal mpMRI is feasible for non-invasive monitoring and may provide complementary information beyond conventional renal function assessment. Trial registration, DRKS, DRKS00018966, registered 10 October 2019; https://www.drks.de/search/de/results

title: Diagnosis and treatment of gastric bronchogenic cyst: a case report and literature review
abstract: Abstract Background: Gastric bronchogenic cyst (GBC) is a rare congenital foregut anomaly, typically located near the gastric fundus or cardia. Due to its nonspecific clinical and imaging features, preoperative diagnosis is challenging, and it is often misdiagnosed as a gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) or other submucosal lesions, especially when imaging reveals a solid-appearing or atypical cystic mass. Case presentation: A 42-year-old asymptomatic woman was incidentally found to have a cystic mass adjacent to the gastric cardia. Enhanced CT and MRI revealed a well-defined, approximately 3.0 cm × 2.2 cm lesion with no significant enhancement. Endoscopy showed a smooth-surfaced submucosal elevation. The patient underwent successful laparoscopic complete resection, with careful dissection to preserve the gastric muscular layer and maintain cyst integrity. Histopathological examination confirmed the diagnosis of GBC, characterized by a cyst wall lined with pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium. The postoperative course was uneventful, and the patient recovered well with no recurrence at the 3-month follow-up. Conclusion: GBC should be considered in the differential diagnosis of a well-defined, non-enhancing cystic mass near the gastric cardia, particularly when it mimics a GIST. Laparoscopic complete resection is a safe and effective approach that enables both definitive diagnosis and curative treatment, with favorable short-term outcomes.

title: Clinical criteria for suspected early hip osteoarthritis at the earliest radiographic stage: an international Technical Expert Panel study
abstract: Abstract Background Early hip osteoarthritis (EHOA) remains challenging to recognise at presentation, particularly when symptoms are recent and radiographic abnormalities are absent or minimal. Standardised clinical criteria for this stage are limited. This study aimed to develop expert-derived criteria for identifying suspected EHOA at the earliest radiographic stage and to propose monitoring suggestions. Methods An international, multidisciplinary Technical Expert Panel study was conducted, supported by a structured literature review and expert panel voting. Candidate items were generated from the literature review and face-to-face expert discussion, then organised into domains and subdomains. Items were included in the final framework when they achieved > 66% agreement. The perceived strength of each retained item was rated on a 0–10 numerical scale. Results The final framework included two overarching areas: criteria for identifying suspected EHOA and suggestions for careful monitoring. Five domains were retained for identification: exclusion/applicability criteria, symptoms and signs, risk factors, time framework and imaging. Key clinical indicators included load-related mechanical pain, pain during hip rotation, brief start-up or morning stiffness, walking limitation and difficulty with squatting, getting in or out of a car, and putting on socks. Supportive risk factors included elevated body mass index, previous hip symptoms, occupational loading, high-level sports participation, previous hip injury or surgery, family history, femoroacetabular impingement, hip dysplasia, Legg-Calve-Perthes disease, slipped capital femoral epiphysis and leg-length discrepancy. A symptom duration of < 6 months was retained as the preferred timeframe. Baseline radiography was emphasised to exclude established OA, while MRI and ultrasound were considered selective complementary tools. Conclusions This Technical Expert Panel proposes a clinical framework for identifying suspected EHOA at the earliest radiographic stage and guiding careful monitoring. Prospective studies are required to validate its diagnostic and prognostic performance before clinical implementation as formal criteria.
