title: Sliding Amyand's hernia with acute appendicitis presenting as an incarcerated inguinoscrotal hernia: a case report
abstract: Abstract Background : Amyand's hernia, defined as the presence of the vermiform appendix within an inguinal hernia sac, is uncommon. Acute appendicitis within an Amyand's hernia is rarer, and a sliding variant in which the caecum contributes to the hernia sac adds further operative complexity. We report a case of sliding Amyand's hernia with acute appendicitis presenting as an incarcerated inguinoscrotal hernia. Case presentation: A 56-year-old man with type 2 diabetes mellitus presented with a one-day history of a painful, irreducible right inguinoscrotal swelling on a background of a three-year hernia. He was constipated but continued to pass flatus and had no fever or urinary symptoms. Examination showed a tender irreducible right inguinoscrotal hernia with a soft, non-tender abdomen and no peritonism. The white cell count was 19 × 10⁹/L and C-reactive protein was 142 mg/L. Plain abdominal radiography showed dilated small bowel loops. Computed tomography was difficult to arrange on an emergency basis. Although ultrasonography was available, it was not requested because the clinical diagnosis of an incarcerated inguinal hernia was sufficiently compelling to warrant operative management, and the anticipated findings were unlikely to alter the decision to proceed with surgery. At exploration, the caecum was found to form part of the wall of the hernia sac within the right hemiscrotum, with a grossly inflamed appendix and inflammatory fluid. There was no features of bowel ischaemia or gangrene. Appendicectomy and primary non-mesh tissue repair were performed. Histology confirmed acute appendicitis. The postoperative course was uncomplicated, and the patient was well at three-week follow-up. Conclusion: Sliding Amyand's hernia with acute appendicitis should be considered as a differential diagnosis in patients presenting with an incarcerated inguinoscrotal hernia and disproportionate inflammatory markers. Although the diagnosis is often established intraoperatively, awareness of this possibility may improve operative preparedness. Intraoperative assessment of appendiceal inflammation, contamination and the sliding caecal anatomy should guide appendiceal management and the choice of hernia repair. In this patient, appendicectomy with primary tissue repair was followed by an uncomplicated early recovery.

title: VIT-DRN-OCAFF: An Optimized Cross-Attention Feature Fusion Framework for Multi- Class COVID-19 and Pulmonary Disease Diagnosis Using Thoracic CT Images
abstract: Abstract Early and accurate pulmonary disease diagnosis remains a major challenge due to the rising prevalence of respiratory infections and chronic lung disorders. The COVID-19 pandemic further emphasized the need for intelligent diagnostic frameworks capable of rapidly identifying pulmonary abnormalities from thoracic Computed Tomography (CT) images. This study proposes a novel Vision Transformer–Dilated Residual Network with Optimized Cross-Attention Feature Fusion (ViT-DRN-OCAFF) framework for multi-class pulmonary disease classification. The proposed architecture combines the global contextual learning capability of Vision Transformers with the lesion-sensitive feature extraction of Dilated Residual Networks, while the Optimized Cross-Attention Feature Fusion (OCAFF) mechanism adaptively refines and integrates complementary pulmonary representations. A comprehensive dataset containing 24,860 thoracic CT images collected from public repositories and collaborating clinical centers was utilized, comprising COVID-19, viral pneumonia, bacterial pneumonia, and non-viral lung abnormalities. Advanced preprocessing techniques, including lung segmentation, adaptive contrast enhancement, lesion-aware normalization, volumetric augmentation, and image refinement, were employed to improve diagnostic feature quality. The Vision Transformer branch captured long-range contextual pulmonary dependencies, whereas the Dilated Residual Network extracted fine-grained pathological features associated with pulmonary lesions. Subsequently, the OCAFF module dynamically prioritized discriminative pulmonary characteristics and minimized redundant activations for improved classification reliability. Experimental evaluation using a 70:15:15 training-validation-testing protocol demonstrated superior performance with 99.42% accuracy, 99.31% precision, 99.27% sensitivity, 99.48% specificity, and 99.29% F1-score, outperforming existing pulmonary disease classification techniques.

title: Profound Depletion of CPB2 and MASP2 Predicts Hepatic Synthetic Collapse and Transplant Indications in HBV-Related Acute Liver Failure
abstract: Abstract Purpose Hepatitis B virus-related acute liver failure (HBV-ALF) is a highly lethal syndrome lacking precise early biomarkers to guide the timing of liver transplantation (LT). Aims We aimed to identify core drivers of hepatic synthetic collapse and explore novel prognostic biomarkers and targeted therapeutic strategies for HBV-ALF. Methods An integrated machine learning framework (LASSO, SVM-RFE) was applied to multi-cohort transcriptomic datasets to identify crucial diagnostic hub genes. Findings were rigorously validated in a real-world clinical cohort of HBV-ALF patients using serum biochemistry and spatial histopathology (H&E and IHC staining). Results We identified a profound disruption of the complement-coagulation crosstalk as a hallmark of HBV-ALF. Three critical hub genes—C8B, CPB2, and MASP2—were significantly downregulated. In clinical validation, CPB2 levels plummeted to approximately 26% of the normal baseline, strongly correlating with declining prothrombin time activity (PTA) and surging MELD scores. Spatial histopathology revealed a paradoxical microenvironment: massive necrosis with a near-complete loss of these locally synthesized proteins, accompanied by intense overactivation of the terminal complement complex (C5b-9) strictly bordering the surviving parenchyma. Conclusions The precipitous depletion of C8B, CPB2, and MASP2 serves as a highly sensitive real-time biomarker for irreversible hepatic synthetic exhaustion, offering a novel metric to refine LT indications. Furthermore, targeting the localized C5b-9 overactivation presents a promising therapeutic strategy to halt the necrotic cascade and serve as a "bridge to transplant" in HBV-ALF.

title: Salvage computed tomography-guided brachytherapy for patients with postoperative vaginal recurrence of endometrial cancer
abstract: Abstract Background This study retrospectively analyzed the treatment outcomes of computed tomography (CT)-guided brachytherapy (BT) for vaginal recurrence after endometrial cancer surgery. Methods Patients with vaginal recurrence after endometrial cancer surgery who underwent CT-guided BT between were retrospectively analyzed. The primary endpoint was local control (LC). Secondary endpoints included regional recurrence-free survival (RRFS), distant metastasis-free survival (DMFS), disease-free survival (DFS), overall survival (OS), and late toxicities. Results 50 patients were included. External beam radiotherapy (EBRT) with a median total dose of 50 Gy was administered to 30 patients. The median number of BT fractions was five for patients with superficial recurrence and three for those with visible recurrence, respectively. The median total dose delivered to the high-risk clinical target volume (HR-CTV) (equivalent dose in 2 Gy fractions; EQD2) was 70.5 Gy. The median follow-up period was 44.8 months. The 3-year LC, RRFS, DMFS, DFS, and OS rates were 85.6%, 82.9%, 65.1%, 46.0%, and 87.1%, respectively. In the univariate analysis, HR-CTV D90 was a significant prognostic factor for LC (p = 0.009). The 3-year LC rate was significantly higher in patients with HR-CTV D90 ≥ 67.3 Gy than in those with < 67.3 Gy (100% vs. 64.2%). In the multivariate analysis, tumor visibility and postoperative risk classification were significant prognostic factors for DMFS (p < 0.011 and p = 0.033, respectively). Conclusions CT-guided BT provides favorable local control in patients with vaginal recurrence after endometrial cancer surgery. However, distant metastases remain a major site of failure. Clinical trial number Not applicable.

title: Cerebral metabolic alterations and network disruption in pulmonary fibrosis assessed with [18F] FDG PET/CT
abstract: Abstract Background Emerging evidence highlights the roles of lung-brain axis in the systemic effects of chronic pulmonary disease, but cerebral metabolic and network manifestations in pulmonary fibrosis (PF) remain poorly characterized. The relationship between cerebral metabolism and clinical outcomes in PF was therefore investigated. Results Compared with healthy controls, patients with PF exhibited hypometabolism in frontal, temporal, insular, cingulate, and caudate regions (all P < 0.05). Significant disruption was identified within the parasympathetic-associated subnetwork ( P < 0.001), whereas no significant alteration was detected in the sympathetic-associated subnetwork ( P = 0.1582). Cerebral metabolism was modestly associated with pulmonary function and systemic inflammatory markers (| r | = 0.213–0.373, P < 0.05). After adjustment for age, sex, forced vital capacity (FVC), and diffusing capacity of the lung for carbon monoxide (DLCO), hypometabolism in selected autonomic and association regions remained associated with poorer EFS (HR = 0.426–0.632, P ≤ 0.048). Conclusions PF was associated with widespread cerebral hypometabolism and metabolic network disruption, particularly within the parasympathetic-associated network. Cerebral metabolic alterations may provide prognostic information beyond conventional pulmonary function measures.

title: Wernicke Encephalopathy Induced by Acute Cholecystitis A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Introduction: Wernicke’s encephalopathy (WE) is an acute central nervous system disorder caused by thiamine deficiency, characterized by a classic triad of ophthalmoplegia, ataxia, and altered mental status. Chronic alcohol use is the most common etiology of WE, but the disease is often misdiagnosed clinically as only a minority of patients exhibit the typical symptoms clearly. Case Report: A patient with acute cholecystitis complicated by WE is reported, who presented with altered consciousness and dysarthria. Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain revealed high signal intensity on fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR) sequences, affecting the dorsolateral brainstem, periaqueductal gray, bilateral thalami, and bilateral parietal lobes. Prior to the onset of neurological symptoms, the patient experienced abdominal pain and loss of appetite due to acute cholecystitis. Suspecting WE, high-dose thiamine treatment was initiated along with rehabilitative functional training. The clinical condition improved rapidly within two weeks. Conclusion In cases of acute cholecystitis accompanied by loss of appetite and fasting, endogenous thiamine reserves can be rapidly depleted. Early adequate parenteral vitamin B1 administration is critical. Additionally, early and tailored rehabilitative interventions for patients exhibiting significant cognitive and muscular impairments are essential for improving prognosis.

Suspecting WE, high-dose thiamine treatment was initiated along with rehabilitative functional training. The clinical condition improved rapidly within two weeks. Conclusion In cases of acute cholecystitis accompanied by loss of appetite and fasting, endogenous thiamine reserves can be rapidly depleted. Early adequate parenteral vitamin B1 administration is critical. Additionally, early and tailored rehabilitative interventions for patients exhibiting significant cognitive and muscular impairments are essential for improving prognosis.

title: Abrupt Onset of Crescentic IgA Nephropathy Superimposed on Glycogen Storage Disease Type Ia: A 15-Year Longitudinal Pediatric Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background Renal involvement is a primary determinant of long-term morbidity in glycogen storage disease type Ia (GSD-Ia). It classically presents as non-immune-mediated metabolic nephropathy that slowly advances from asymptomatic glomerular hyperfiltration to focal segmental glomerulosclerosis. The concurrence of an immune-complex glomerulopathy is exceptionally rare. We report the first pediatric case of GSD-Ia complicated by biopsy-proven crescentic IgA nephropathy followed longitudinally over 15 years, shedding light on the diagnostic vigilance and therapeutic adaptations required for superimposed glomerulonephritis. Case presentation: A 15-year-old male with genetically confirmed GSD-Ia had a history of early glomerular hyperfiltration, recurrent nephrolithiasis, and low-grade proteinuria since age 4, remaining clinically stable for over six years on dietary management and angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors. At 11 years of age, despite well-controlled metabolic parameters, he abruptly developed nephrotic-range proteinuria (urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio: 7207.5 mg/g Cr; 24-hour urine protein: 4483.8 mg) and hematuria. Given this sharp deviation from typical metabolic nephropathy, a percutaneous renal biopsy was performed. Histopathology revealed chronic tubulointerstitial injury superimposed with crescentic IgA nephropathy featuring cellular and fibrocellular crescents in 7 of 25 glomeruli, strong mesangial IgA deposition, and confluent electron-dense deposits. Induction therapy with oral glucocorticoids and mycophenolate mofetil markedly reduced proteinuria. Due to residual proteinuria, treatment was transitioned to low-dose glucocorticoids combined with tacrolimus, which successfully achieved clinical remission. All immunosuppressants were discontinued by early 2026. At the 15-year follow-up, the patient maintained durable clinical remission with preserved renal function (serum creatinine: 31 µmol/L; urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio: 1051.3 mg/g Cr). Conclusions In patients with GSD-Ia, an abrupt onset of nephrotic-range proteinuria strongly warrants suspicion of superimposed glomerulonephritis rather than intrinsic metabolic nephropathy alone. Prompt renal biopsy is essential to establish an accurate diagnosis. Combining tight metabolic control with targeted calcineurin inhibitor-based immunosuppressive therapy represents an effective dual-track strategy to induce remission and preserve long-term renal function in this complex scenario.

title: Translating Imaging-based Brain Age Models for Predicting Accelerated Brain Ageing in African Populations: A Pilot Study on a Nigerian Cohort.
abstract: Abstract Background: Brain age is an emerging imaging biomarker for early detection of neurodegenerative disorders, based on the estimation of the brain’s biological age. Existing predictive models are predominantly trained on Global North (GN) neuroimaging data, limiting their sensitivity when applied to underrepresented populations due to geographic, imaging scanner, and biological heterogeneity. We investigated this bias by adapting the standard Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) method to a population-specific (PS) brain age model. Methods: Using a multi-institutional T1-weighted brain MRI dataset from 309 Nigerian adults, we implemented a robust low-compute image analysis pipeline which includes repurposing clinical scans and high-resolution cortical parcellation with multi-stage quality control. The PS-GPR model was trained on regional brain volumetric features from the Nigerian MRI scans and its performance compared to four common GN pre-trained models. Results: The proposed PS-GPR model showed a significantly lower prediction error (mean absolute error = 9.82 years) without age-bias correction and few seconds inference time compared to GN-trained machine learning models (mean absolute error = 10.00 – 16.70 years). SPARROW, a generalizable deep learning framework achieved an MAE of 7.87 but failed on 6% of the test set. This early work demonstrates the importance of representative data to build resource-efficient clinically viable models. Conclusion: This population-specific model is a step towards sensitive low-compute African brain age models. With the expansion of imaging data beyond Nigeria through the Africa Neuroimaging Archive (AfNiA), we will further develop the PS model to identify individuals with accelerated brain ageing for early intervention in at-risk adults.

title: Giant supraclavicular schwannoma involving the cervical nerve root: surgical management and perioperative neurological monitoring—a case report
abstract: Abstract Objective To describe the clinical features, surgical management, and postoperative neurological outcomes of a giant right supraclavicular schwannoma extending toward the cervical intervertebral foramen. Particular attention was paid to the tumor’s close relationship with the surrounding neurovascular structures. Methods We retrospectively reviewed the clinical data, imaging findings, surgical procedures, pathological findings, postoperative course, and follow-up of a patient with a giant right supraclavicular schwannoma. The surgical and perioperative management was evaluated with regard to the tumor’s relationship to adjacent neurovascular structures, intraoperative blood loss, postoperative neurological function, wound and drainage status, and recovery. The case was reported in accordance with the CARE guidelines[1]. Results A 47-year-old woman was admitted after an incidentally detected neck mass had persisted for more than 1 month. Imaging revealed a mixed-density mass with abnormal signal in the right supraclavicular region, measuring approximately 58 mm at its largest diameter. The lesion extended toward the right intervertebral foramen, with prominent vessels surrounding the mass. Preoperative biopsy showed a spindle cell tumor consistent with schwannoma. Immunohistochemistry was positive for S-100 and SOX10, with a Ki-67 index of approximately 3%[11]. The patient underwent right cervical soft-tissue tumor resection, vascular and nerve exploration and neurolysis, and random-pattern fascial flap reconstruction. Intraoperative blood loss was approximately 400 ml, and 1.5 U of packed red blood cells and 220 ml of plasma were transfused. A wound drain was placed after surgery. Postoperative management included cervical compression with a salt bag, monitoring of the wound and drainage, and serial neurological assessments. No postoperative wound bleeding or cervical hematoma developed. Numbness in the distal phalanges of the right hand gradually improved, muscle strength remained grade V, and distal limb perfusion was preserved. The patient was discharged on postoperative day 5 with satisfactory wound healing. At 1 month after surgery, cervical MRI showed slight enlargement of the right C6/7 nerve root. The patient had no cervical scar tenderness or other significant symptoms. Conclusion Giant supraclavicular schwannomas can be difficult to remove because of their deep location and close proximity to major vessels, peripheral nerves, and cervical nerve roots. Preoperative imaging, careful dissection, and postoperative neurological assessment are important for reducing complications and preserving neurological function. Perioperative management should be tailored to the tumor anatomy and intraoperative findings rather than based solely on routine risk scores[5][6][7][8][9][10].

title: Development and Internal Validation of a CBCT-Integrated Prognostic Nomogram for Tooth Survival in Periodontal-Endodontic Combined Lesions: A 5-Year Retrospective Cohort Study Running title: CBCT-integrated nomogram for tooth survival in perio-endo lesions
abstract: Abstract Aim To identify clinical, CBCT-based radiographic, and patient-level predictors of 5-year tooth survival in periodontal-endodontic (perio-endo) combined lesions and develop an internally validated prognostic nomogram. Methods This retrospective cohort included 288 teeth from 288 patients with perio-endo combined lesions and ≥ 5 years of follow-up. Time to extraction was analysed using Kaplan–Meier estimation and multivariable Cox regression, with backward elimination from 14 candidate predictors. A points-based nomogram was developed from the final model. Discrimination was assessed using Harrell's C-index with 500 bootstrap resamples, and calibration compared predicted and observed 5-year survival across risk quintiles. Results Seventy-nine teeth (27.4%) were extracted, with a median time to extraction of 30 months. Overall 5-year survival was 72.6% (95% CI, 67.4–77.7%). Survival differed by lesion class, mobility, and furcation involvement. Independent predictors of extraction were inadequate root canal obturation (HR 2.41), greater mobility (HR 1.64 per grade), furcation involvement (HR 1.45 per grade), probing depth (HR 1.30/mm), CBCT volumetric bone loss (HR 1.0054/mm³), diabetes mellitus (HR 1.87), and poorer oral hygiene (HR 1.02/%). The nomogram showed good discrimination (apparent C-index 0.812; bootstrap-corrected 0.802) and close agreement between predicted and observed 5-year survival. Conclusion A CBCT-integrated nomogram combining seven clinical, radiographic, and patient-level variables provided accurate individualised prediction of 5-year tooth survival in perio-endo combined lesions. External validation is required before routine clinical implementation.

title: Computed Tomography–Based Assessment of the Congruency of Precontoured Anatomical Clavicle Plates in the Indian Population: A Hospital-Based Observational Study
abstract: Abstract Purpose Precontoured anatomical clavicle plates are designed predominantly from Western morphometric data, and ethnic variation in clavicular anatomy may compromise plate-to-bone congruency in Indian patients. This study evaluated the congruency of a precontoured anatomical clavicle plate in an Indian population using computed tomography (CT)-based mathematical modelling and the Clavicle Congruence Score (CCS). Methods In this hospital-based observational study conducted at a tertiary care hospital in South India between May 2024 and October 2025, adult patients undergoing CT of the thorax or neck were included after applying predefined eligibility criteria. Three-dimensional reconstructions were used to derive clavicular morphometric parameters, and a commercially available anatomical clavicle plate was virtually superimposed on each reconstruction to measure vertical plate-to-bone gap and anterior and posterior overhang. Plate fit was graded by the CCS as anatomical, good or poor. Results Twenty-two clavicles from 22 participants (mean age 44.6 ± 16.3 years; 63.6% male) were analysed. Mean clavicular length was 143.6 ± 10.8 mm. Mean vertical plate-to-bone gap was 2.4 ± 1.6 mm, with mean anterior and posterior overhang of 1.8 ± 1.4 mm and 2.0 ± 1.5 mm, respectively. CCS grading showed anatomical fit in 27.3%, good fit in 45.4% and poor fit in 27.3% of clavicles. Conclusion Considerable morphological variability was observed, and the evaluated plate did not achieve anatomical fit in a substantial proportion of Indian clavicles, supporting preoperative anatomical assessment and population-specific implant design. Level of Evidence: Level IV, observational study.

title: Superior mesenteric artery syndrome associated with recurrent aspiration and difficult ventilator liberation in a post-trauma patient: a case report
abstract: Abstract Background: Superior mesenteric artery syndrome (SMAS) is an uncommon cause of proximal intestinal obstruction caused by compression of the third portion of the duodenum between the superior mesenteric artery and the aorta. Recurrent vomiting can result in aspiration and respiratory deterioration. We report SMAS as a potentially reversible gastrointestinal contributor to recurrent aspiration and repeated difficulty in ventilator liberation in a critically ill post-trauma patient. Case presentation: A 19-year-old Saudi male with severe traumatic brain injury after a road traffic accident was transferred for prolonged ventilatory care after craniectomy, ventriculoperitoneal shunt placement, right elbow fixation, and tracheostomy. At transfer, his Glasgow Coma Scale score was 7/15; height was 167 cm and weight 70 kg (BMI 25.1 kg/m²). During approximately 12 months of ventilator dependence, five attempts to transition from pressure-regulated volume control (PRVC) to continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) failed after episodes of vomiting followed by aspiration pneumonia, documented by new chest-radiographic opacity and increased ventilatory requirements. Chest and abdominal radiographs demonstrated marked gastric distension. Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT in November demonstrated compression of the third part of the duodenum at the aortomesenteric region with severe proximal gastroduodenal dilatation. Retrospective review showed a narrowed aortomesenteric angle of approximately 20–25° and a minimum aortomesenteric distance of approximately 7 mm. Approximately one week after diagnosis, a jejunal extension was placed endoscopically through the existing PEG (PEG-J) beyond the obstructed segment. Vomiting ceased, and the patient was liberated from mechanical ventilation within one week. He remained off ventilator support for one year of follow-up, with no recurrence of vomiting. Conclusions: In neurologically impaired or post-trauma patients with persistent vomiting, marked gastric distension, recurrent aspiration, or otherwise unexplained difficulty in ventilator liberation, SMAS should be considered among reversible extrapulmonary contributors. An enlarged stomach on routine chest radiography is nonspecific but may prompt definitive abdominal imaging. In selected patients, post-pyloric feeding through a PEG-J can bypass the obstruction and control vomiting. The temporal association between cessation of vomiting and durable ventilator liberation in this case supports contribution from SMAS but does not establish sole causality.

title: FLNC-related myopathy: a description of 27 patients from 21 unrelated families
abstract: Abstract Myofibrillar myopathies are inherited neuromuscular disorders characterized by protein aggregation and myofibrillar disorganization. FLNC -related myopathy, a subtype of MFM, encompasses a broad clinical spectrum ranging from limb-girdle and distal myopathies to isolated cardiomyopathy. We retrospectively collected a cohort of 27 patients with genetically confirmed FLNC- related myopathy. Mean age at first symptoms and diagnosis was 40 ± 14 and 54 ± 17 years, respectively. Among the 27 patients, 13 (48%) had proximal muscle weakness only, 3 (11%) had distal muscle weakness only, 9 (33%) had both proximal and distal weakness, and 2 (8%) had no limb weakness. Axial weakness was identified in 16 patients (59%), facial weakness in 4 patients (15%), cardiac involvement such as cardiomyopathies (hypertrophic or dilated) in 13 patients (48%), and conduction and rhythm disorders requiring an implantable cardioverter defibrillator in 2 patients. Mean value of forced vital capacity was 85 ± 28% and 3 patients with sleep apnea syndrome required nocturnal CPAP. Muscle magnetic resonance imaging showed fatty replacement mainly in thigh muscles affecting the posterior compartment, pelvic girdle, and paravertebral muscles. Mean creatine kinase value was 502 ± 436 U/L. Muscle biopsy showed muscle fiber size variability, intracytoplasmic protein aggregates, internalized nuclei, rimmed vacuoles and type 1 muscle fiber predominance. FLNC gene analysis identified heterozygous missense and nonsense variants in 22 (81%) and 3 (11%) patients respectively, and a complex deletion insertion variant in 2 patients (7%). This study reports one of the largest multicenter cohorts of FLNC -related myopathy, confirming that the disease most frequently presents as an adult-onset proximal myopathy with frequent cardiac involvement. We also identified a relatively consistent MRI pattern mainly involving the posterior thigh and paravertebral muscles. Despite the predominance of missense FLNC variants, substantial clinical and pathological heterogeneity was observed, with no clear genotype–phenotype correlation.

title: Long-term prognostic value and clinical correlates of brain [¹⁸F]-FDG PET in patients with post-COVID-19 condition and neurocognitive disorders: a prospective cohort study
abstract: Abstract Purpose : Brain [18F]-FDG-PET often reveals cerebral hypometabolism in post-COVID-19 patients experiencing neurocognitive issues, but its prognostic value remains uncertain. We evaluated the long-term utility of [18F]-FDG PET in this population. Materials and Methods: We reviewed the prospective SYNPOCov cohort (NCT05610436), including WHO-defined post-COVID-19 patients with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 who underwent brain PET scans and had ≥1 year of follow-up. Final clinical outcomes were adjudicated as good (no residual disability), partial (improvement but persistent disability), or stable by an expert adjudication committee. PET scans were compared with those of age- and sex-matched pre-pandemic healthy controls (n=39). Regional metabolic values were extracted from significant clusters (voxel-level p < 0.005; cluster-level p < 0.05, FWE-corrected) and associated with demographic and clinical data. Results: Seventy patients were included (48.3±11.9 years; 69% female; 26.4 ± 9.5 months follow-up), of whom 19, 34, and 17 were classified as having good, partial, and stable clinical outcomes respectively. Baseline imaging demonstrated hypometabolism in four clusters: right frontal, parietal and lateral temporal cortex, and cerebellum. Metabolic values in the right frontal and lateral temporal clusters were significantly lower in previously hospitalized patients and with pre-Omicron variants (p=≤0.04 and p=≤0.03 respectively). However, neither baseline regional metabolism nor its longitudinal evolution on follow-up PET scans (n=30) was associated with long-term clinical outcome. Conclusion: Brain [¹⁸F]-FDG PET remains a valuable biomarker of cerebral involvement in post-COVID-19 neurocognitive disorder, revealing metabolic signatures associated with acute disease severity and viral variant. While not predictive of long-term outcome, PET findings improve understanding of factors underlying persistent cerebral dysfunction. Trial registration number and date of registration: NCT05610436; 2022-01-07

Final clinical outcomes were adjudicated as good (no residual disability), partial (improvement but persistent disability), or stable by an expert adjudication committee. PET scans were compared with those of age- and sex-matched pre-pandemic healthy controls (n=39). Regional metabolic values were extracted from significant clusters (voxel-level p < 0.005; cluster-level p < 0.05, FWE-corrected) and associated with demographic and clinical data. Results: Seventy patients were included (48.3±11.9 years; 69% female; 26.4 ± 9.5 months follow-up), of whom 19, 34, and 17 were classified as having good, partial, and stable clinical outcomes respectively. Baseline imaging demonstrated hypometabolism in four clusters: right frontal, parietal and lateral temporal cortex, and cerebellum. Metabolic values in the right frontal and lateral temporal clusters were significantly lower in previously hospitalized patients and with pre-Omicron variants (p=≤0.04 and p=≤0.03 respectively). However, neither baseline regional metabolism nor its longitudinal evolution on follow-up PET scans (n=30) was associated with long-term clinical outcome. Conclusion: Brain [¹⁸F]-FDG PET remains a valuable biomarker of cerebral involvement in post-COVID-19 neurocognitive disorder, revealing metabolic signatures associated with acute disease severity and viral variant. While not predictive of long-term outcome, PET findings improve understanding of factors underlying persistent cerebral dysfunction. title: Striatal tissue iron in depressed and healthy individuals and the effect of buproprion
abstract: Abstract Introduction: Dopaminergic dysfunction in the striatum is thought to play a central role in anhedonia in major depressive disorder (MDD). Normalised T2*-weighted (nT2*w) imaging provides a widely available MRI-derived proxy of striatal tissue iron, an indirect marker of dopaminergic function, but its relationship with reward processing and anhedonia in MDD has not been established. In this secondary analysis, we examined whether striatal nT2*w distinguishes individuals with MDD from healthy controls, is associated with reward learning and clinical symptoms, including anhedonia and depression, and is sensitive to treatment with the dopaminergic antidepressant bupropion Methods Depressed (n = 40) and healthy participants (n = 41) underwent clinical assessment, functional MRI, and a probabilistic instrumental learning task (PILT) at baseline, with follow-up assessments after 2 and 6 weeks. Participants with MDD received open-label bupropion treatment throughout the 6-week study. The primary outcome was MRI-derived striatal tissue iron, quantified using nT2*w signal extracted from resting-state fMRI within the whole striatum, caudate, putamen, and nucleus accumbens. Associations between nT2*w, diagnostic group, reward learning, clinical symptoms, and treatment response were examined. Results At baseline, depressed participants compared to healthy controls showed significantly higher striatal and caudate nT2*w values, indicative of lower tissue iron. The marker demonstrated excellent 2-week test-retest reliability in healthy participants. Striatal nT2*w was not associated with reward learning, anhedonia, or depression severity at baseline, and did not change following 2 weeks of bupropion treatment or predict clinical response after 6 weeks. Across groups, females demonstrated higher nT2*w values (lower tissue iron) than males in the striatum, caudate, and putamen. Discussion Striatal nT2*w represents a promising, robust and widely accessible neuroimaging marker of depression, reliably distinguishing depressed individuals from healthy controls while demonstrating excellent test–retest reliability. Larger longitudinal studies are now needed to establish its clinical utility and determine whether it can detect changes in reward processing and treatment response across the course of illness.

title: Assessment of Atrioventricular and Ventriculoarterial Coupling Indices in Patients with Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome Utilizing Cardiac MRI and Invasive Hemodynamics
abstract: Abstract Background Atrioventricular (AV) and ventriculoarterial (VA) coupling indices have demonstrated prognostic value in various cardiac pathologies but have not been studied in hypoplastic left heart syndrome (HLHS). This study assessed known and novel AV and VA coupling indices derived from cardiac MRI (CMR) and invasive hemodynamics for predicting adverse outcomes in HLHS patients with stage II palliation prior to Fontan completion. Methods CMR and catheterization data from 45 HLHS patients with stage II palliation undergoing pre-Fontan evaluation (January 2015–October 2025) were retrospectively analyzed. Known AV coupling indices and two novel indices—RA SV -RV coupling index (RA stroke volume indexed/RV end-diastolic volume indexed) and combined RA-RV-Aorta coupling index—were compared between patients with and without adverse outcomes (composite of death, transplantation, heart failure hospitalization, SGLT2 inhibitor initiation, plastic bronchitis, protein-losing enteropathy). Predictive performance was assessed using Firth logistic regression and ROC analysis. Results Ten patients (22%) experienced adverse outcomes. Known AV coupling indices did not significantly differ between groups (AUC 0.48–0.69). The RV-Aortic coupling index was significantly lower in the adverse outcomes group (0.17 vs. 0.23, p = 0.006; AUC = 0.80). Both novel indices demonstrated superior discrimination: RA SV -RV (0.11 vs. 0.17, p = 0.002; AUC = 0.82) and novel RAsv-RV-Aorta (2.13 vs. 3.90, p = 0.001; AUC = 0.86). Nested models showed that adding each novel index to RV-Aortic coupling significantly improved model fit (p = 0.036 and p = 0.048, respectively). Conclusions Novel coupling indices designed for single ventricle physiology outperformed known AV coupling indices and provided incremental predictive value beyond RV-Aortic coupling alone for adverse outcomes in HLHS patients with stage II palliation.

title: Primary Solitary Fibrous Tumor of the Lacrimal Sac Mimicking Lymphoma: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background: Primary solitary fibrous tumor (SFT) of the lacrimal sac is among the rarest presentations of this mesenchymal neoplasm. We report a patient in whom the mass was initially dismissed as chronic dacryocystitis during three months of conservative therapy, and an outside magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) report suggested lymphoma. The diagnosis was ultimately resolved by signal transducer and activator of transcription 6 (STAT6) immunohistochemistry performed on the resected tissue. Case presentation: A 50-year-old Chinese man was referred with a two-year history of a painless, slowly growing right medial canthal mass. After three months of unsuccessful antibiotic and warm-compress therapy for presumed chronic dacryocystitis at another hospital, imaging raised concern for lymphoma. We performed complete excision via an external approach together with bicanalicular intubation. Histology revealed a spindle-cell tumor with alternating cellularity. Diffuse nuclear STAT6 positivity confirmed SFT. At one month, the lacrimal drainage system was patent without evidence of recurrence. Conclusions: Lacrimal sac SFT closely mimics both chronic dacryocystitis clinically and lymphoma radiologically. When antibiotics and warm compresses fail to shrink a medial canthal mass, early biopsy rather than observation is warranted. In our practice, STAT6 staining has become the most reliable way to distinguish SFT from tumors that look identical under the microscope. Complete local excision with concurrent bicanalicular intubation can remove the tumor and restore drainage in a single procedure.

title: Construction of a Retinopathy of Prematurity Onset Prediction Model Using the Random Forest Machine Learning Algorithm
abstract: Abstract Objective: This study aimed to refine and validate a previously developed Random Forest prediction model for the onset of Retinopathy of Prematurity (ROP), which was based on a machine learning approach. Methods: A retrospective study was conducted on 150 neonatal cases who met the inclusion criteria and underwent ROP screening at the Department of Neonatology, Wuzhou Workers' Hospital, Guangxi, China, between January 2024 and September 2024.1.Data on ROP-related risk factors and concurrent fundus screening results were collected by reviewing the electronic medical records (inpatient and follow-up outpatient) of the enrolled neonates.2.The top 15 risk factors identified from five distinct machine learning models were analyzed to identify the common risk factors among them.3.The Random Forest prediction model was validated. Results: 1.Nine common risk factors were identified from the top 15 factors across the five machine learning models: oxygen therapy, oxygen concentration, gestational age, birth weight, anemia of prematurity, neonatal respiratory distress syndrome (NRDS), necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC), in vitro fertilization embryo transfer, and antibiotic use.2.Validation of the Random Forest model using the dataset from Wuzhou Workers' Hospital showed good performance on the validation set: AUC: 0.892, accuracy: 77.9%, specificity: 99.3%, sensitivity: 62.9%, precision: 89.9%. Conclusion: The Random Forest model, constructed using machine learning methods and incorporating predictive features such as oxygen therapy, oxygen concentration, gestational age, birth weight, anemia of prematurity, NRDS, NEC, in vitro fertilization embryo transfer, and antibiotic use, demonstrates good predictive value for ROP. This model holds potential for application in clinical screening of high-risk populations for retinopathy of prematurity.

title: Material selection for a 3D-printed tissue-equivalent cost-effective phantom for radiotherapy quality assurance
abstract: Abstract Background and Aims: Patient-specific 3D-printed phantoms are increasingly used for radiotherapy quality assurance (QA) because they are cost-effective and reproduce individual patient anatomy. A major challenge is identifying materials that mimic human tissue.In this work we systematically evaluate radiological properties of various commonly available and industrial 3D printing materials, whereby we include a combined characterization at diagnostic (keV) and therapeutic (MeV) photon energies. Methods and Materials: Over 60 cubes of plastic samples of about 30 materials and different in-fill densities were printed using three different filament printers. CT scans were acquired and the average Hounsfield Units (HU) for each sample was determined. Massdensities (ρm), electron density (ρe), and relative electron density (RED) were assessed. All samples were compared with ICRU reference data. The response at therapeutic energies was evaluated by irradiating the samples and measuring the deposited dose using a micro-diamond detector. These were compared with Pinnacle TPS predictions. Results: The tested materials with 100% filling showed HU values between -95.52 and 238.63. The ρm, ρe, and RED values ranged from 0.963 to 1.228 g/cm3, 3.128 to 3.898 ×1023 and 0.935 to 1.166, respectively. Deviations between measured and TPS dose ranged from -1.34% to 1.36%. Several materials matched ICRU soft-tissue specification. By varying the in-fill density of the materials, refinements could be realized. Conclusions: By combining CT-based characterization with MeV dosimetric validation and testing materials from multiple printing technologies, we identified several candidate plastics suitable for soft-tissue-equivalent radiotherapy phantoms. These can be printed using moderately priced 3D printers (<∼5k euro).

title: Correlation Between Demographic Data and Intraoperative Distal Femoral Anthropometry in Patients Undergoing Total Knee Arthroplasty
abstract: Abstract Background : Accurate prediction of femoral component size is important, particularly in populations with diverse anthropometry. Radiographic templating is resource-intensive. Demographic parameters may offer a simple alternative, but data from African populations are scarce. Objectives: To determine the correlation between demographic data and intraoperative distal femoral anthropometric measurements in patients undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty (TKA). Methods : This cross-sectional study included 78 consecutive patients undergoing primary TKA for osteoarthritis at a regional Orthopaedic Hospital in Nigeria between May 2024 and April 2025. Preoperative age, sex, height, weight and BMI were recorded. Intraoperatively, anteroposterior diameter (fAPD) and mediolateral width (fMLW) of the resected distal femur were measured using a Vernier caliper. Pearson correlation and multivariate linear regression were performed using SPSS v28. Results : Mean age was 66.12 ± 6.30 years. Mean fAPD was 58.65 ± 5.95 mm and fMLW was 70.11 ± 6.91 mm. Female sex predicted both fAPD [B = -4.801, β = -.283, p =.021] and fMLW [B = -8.310, β = -.420, p <.001]. Height predicted fAPD [B = 139.245, β = 1.760, p =.045], and age independently predicted fMLW [B = -.230, β = -.210, p =.028]. The fAPD model was significant [F (5,72) = 3.84, p =.004, R² = 0.211]. The fMLW model was significant [F (5,72) = 8.10, p <.001, R² = 0.428]. Weight and BMI were not significant predictors. Conclusion: In this Nigerian cohort, intraoperative distal femoral dimensions were primarily determined by sex, with additional contributions from height for APD and age for MLW. These findings support consideration of sex, age, and height in preoperative planning for TKA. Level of Evidence: III

title: Quadratus Lumborum Block for Robotic Prostatectomy: Improved Early Recovery but Not Short-Term Event-Free Survival — A Randomized Trial
abstract: Abstract Objective : This randomized, double-blind trial investigated whether adding a quadratus lumborum block (QLB) to general anesthesia (GA) improves 6‑month event‑free survival (EFS) and recovery after robot‑assisted laparoscopic radical prostatectomy (RALP). Methods : Three hundred fifty patients were randomized; the modified intention-to-treat population comprised 299 patients (GA+QLB, n=148; GA alone, n=151). The primary outcome was 6‑month EFS (composite of biochemical/radiographic recurrence or initiation of salvage/adjuvant therapy). Secondary outcomes included opioid consumption, pain scores, quality of recovery, and inflammatory markers. Results : Baseline characteristics were available for the per-protocol population (n=286). Within the confines of this trial, we did not detect a statistically significant difference in 6-month EFS between the GA+QLB and GA groups (adjusted HR = 0.858, 95% CI: 0.572–1.285, P = 0.457). However, the GA+QLB group demonstrated clinically meaningful improvements in early recovery outcomes, including significantly lower intraoperative opioid consumption, lower postoperative pain scores, shorter time to first flatus, and higher QoR‑40 scores on postoperative day 1 (all P < 0.05). Inflammatory and immune markers showed no significant intergroup differences. Conclusion : In this randomized trial, adding QLB to GA did not improve the 6‑month composite EFS endpoint for RALP. While the oncologic effect remains inconclusive and requires longer follow‑up, the study provides robust evidence that QLB significantly enhances early recovery—reducing opioid use and improving patient‑reported quality of recovery. These benefits support routine inclusion of QLB in multimodal analgesia for RALP within ERAS pathways. Trial registration : Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR); Identifier: [ChiCTR-2200066968]; Date of registration: December 22, 2022; Prospectively registered.

title: CogAlign-CausalX: mask-grounded polyp analysis with closed-form explanation-alignment scoring
abstract: Abstract Deep networks segment colonoscopic polyps with Dice coefficients above 0.90, but the explanations offered alongside those segmentations remain qualitative. We describe CogAlign-CausalX, a pipeline in which the explanation is a structural property of the computation rather than a post-hoc attribution. An EfficientNet-B0/U-Net segmenter produces a probability map binarised at a threshold frozen on the validation split; the binary mask gates the input image by Hadamard product, and a ResNet-18 head assigns a three-tier morphological label from the gated pixels alone. Because the classifier sees only the masked region, the mask is the explanation, and scoring it against expert annotation scores the explanation directly. We do this with XAlign, a closed-form measure combining regional concentration, boundary adherence and a dispersion penalty. On a stratified 700/150/150 partition of Kvasir-SEG with MD5-verified disjointness, the pipeline reached a test Dice of 0.8472 (95% CI 0.8191–0.8744), an IoU of 0.7652, a tier accuracy of 0.8067 and an alignment score of 0.8404 (0.8127–0.8674). Alignment scoring cost 0.42 ms per image against 16.4 s for thirty-pass Monte-Carlo dropout. All twenty-nine tier errors fell between adjacent tiers. Two findings run against the proposal. The alignment score has no false-negative term, so a conservative prediction lying wholly inside the lesion scores 0.982 while its Dice is 0.667; the score must be read beside an overlap measure, never in place of one. Segmentation accuracy also sits roughly seven Dice points below current transformer and state-space baselines, and all results derive from a single training seed on a single partition.

title: Complicated Sigmoid Diverticular Disease Presenting as Extensive Retroperitoneal and Thigh Necrotizing Soft-Tissue Infection: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Introduction: Necrotizing soft-tissue infection (NSTI) is a rare, rapidly progressive, and potentially fatal surgical emergency. Early diagnosis is challenging due to its nonspecific presentation, and prompt recognition followed by urgent imaging and surgical intervention is essential to improve outcome. Case presentation: A 57 year old woman presented with generalized weakness, poor oral intake, lower abdominal pain, and oliguria. She was hypotensive, hypoxic, and in acute kidney injury with metabolic acidosis. Non-contrast CT revealed complicated sigmoid diverticulitis with extensive extraluminal gas extending through the left retroperitoneum, psoas, pelvis, and thigh, consistent with an extensive necrotizing soft-tissue infection. Emergency laparotomy with resection of the diseased sigmoid colon, upper rectum, distal ileum, and cecum, followed by end ileostomy and colostomy, was performed along with extensive left thigh exploration and debridement. Despite initial improvement following source control and intensive care, she developed wound infection with carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae and progressive hemodynamic deterioration, ultimately dying of cardiac arrest on postoperative day 19. Conclusion This case highlights the challenges of recognizing deep necrotizing infection from an intra-abdominal source, emphasizing the importance of early imaging and surgical source control.

title: Cross-Scale Micro-CT Super-Resolution for Digital Rock Reconstruction in Heterogeneous Conglomerate Reservoirs
abstract: Abstract Accurate cross-scale characterization of heterogeneous reservoirs is needed for digital-rock analysis, hydrocarbon production, and subsurface energy storage assessment. Micro-computed tomography (micro-CT) faces a field-of-view-resolution trade-off: large-volume scans capture gravel-scale heterogeneity but miss pore-scale features. This study presents Hy-MambaIR, a hybrid Mamba-Transformer network for super-resolution reconstruction of micro-CT images from heterogeneous conglomerate reservoirs. A local-to-global serial architecture combines windowed self-attention and dynamic Tanh normalization for fine-pore recovery with Mamba-based global modeling and spatial-channel attention for large-scale gravel structures. The model was evaluated with paired multi-resolution micro-CT images and against representative convolutional and Transformer baselines. Hy-MambaIR achieved a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 33.36 dB, exceeding HAT by 1.31 dB, and reached 30 dB with 6.6-fold fewer training iterations than HAT. Physical validation showed that the reconstructed images preserved segmentation accuracy, pore topology, pore-throat distributions, and single-phase flow fields; the mean relative error of three-directional absolute permeability on the 855^3-voxel representative elementary volume was 18.56%. Supervised fine-tuning on pebbly sandstone reduced this MRE to 3.59%. These results establish a computational route for physically informed digital-rock reconstruction and reservoir characterization in heterogeneous geoenergy systems.

title: Multifocal Well-Differentiated Small Intestinal Neuroendocrine Tumor Presenting as Partial Small Bowel Obstruction in an Elderly Female: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background Small intestinal neuroendocrine tumors (SI-NETs) are rare, slow-growing malignancies that frequently present with nonspecific gastrointestinal symptoms, leading to diagnostic delays averaging five to seven years. Despite the existence of blood-based biomarkers including serum chromogranin A and urinary 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid (5-HIAA), most patients continue to present with advanced locoregional or metastatic disease. This case illustrates the diagnostic and surgical challenges of SI-NET in an elderly patient and highlights the clinical consequences of delayed biomarker utilization. Case presentation: A 77-year-old White female was referred to a surgical clinic after her primary care physician identified a small bowel mass on imaging ordered for chronic abdominal discomfort and a 20-pound unintentional weight loss. CT imaging demonstrated a solid mesenteric mass with adjacent adenopathy and small bowel tethering, producing the characteristic spoke-wheel sign of mesenteric desmoplasia. Serum chromogranin A and urinary 5-HIAA were not obtained prior to surgical referral. She underwent exploratory laparotomy with open small bowel resection and side-to-side anastomosis. Surgical pathology confirmed multifocal, well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumor (Grade 1, Ki-67 ~ 1%), staged pT4N1, with lymphovascular and perineural invasion and a positive mesenteric margin. Postoperative Dotatate PET identified a single PET-avid mesenteric lesion, prompting referral to a tertiary hepatobiliary center. A second exploratory laparotomy resected a 1.5 cm mesenteric nodule requiring direct repair of a superior mesenteric artery branch. Final pathology demonstrated fibrosis and chronic inflammation with no residual neuroendocrine tumor. The patient elected active surveillance with annual follow-up. Conclusions This case demonstrates the striking discordance between low tumor grade and advanced locoregional disease extent in SI-NETs and underscores the missed opportunity for earlier detection through routine biomarker screening in symptomatic patients. The PET-positive mesenteric nodule that yielded only fibrosis on re-resection raises important questions about functional imaging specificity in the desmoplastic postoperative mesentery. Clinicians should maintain a low threshold for obtaining serum chromogranin A and urinary 5-HIAA in patients presenting with unexplained weight loss and chronic gastrointestinal symptoms.

title: HeteroSurv: Multiview Computed Tomography Radiomics for Continuous Survival-Time Prediction in Immunotherapy-Treated Advanced Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
abstract: Abstract Background Reliable pretreatment markers are needed to identify patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer who are likely to have early progression or shortened survival after immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy. This study developed and validated a computed tomography-based radiomics model to quantify heterogeneity within and around primary lung tumors and to predict progression-free survival and overall survival. Methods This multicenter retrospective study included 414 patients from three hospitals. Baseline contrast-enhanced computed tomography scans obtained within 28 days before treatment were processed with a standardized workflow. Primary tumors were manually segmented, and imaging features were extracted from the whole tumor, a surrounding peritumoral region, subregional tumor textures, and intratumoral heterogeneity patterns. These complementary imaging views were combined using a multiview fusion method, and separate survival models were built for progression-free survival and overall survival. The model was trained in 157 patients and tested in a validation cohort of 52 patients, an internal test cohort of 52 patients, and two external cohorts of 50 and 103 patients. Results The fused imaging score separated patients into high-risk and low-risk groups for both outcomes in every cohort. In the two external cohorts, the concordance index was 0.659 and 0.607 for progression-free survival and 0.709 and 0.716 for overall survival. At 24 months, the time-dependent receiver operating characteristic area under the curve ranged from 0.646 to 0.888 for progression-free survival and from 0.711 to 0.940 for overall survival across the training and test cohorts. Calibration and decision curve analyses supported the model’s agreement and possible clinical utility. Conclusions This pretreatment computed tomography-based multiview radiomics signature could provide a noninvasive approach to risk assessment in advanced non-small cell lung cancer treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors, but prospective validation is needed before clinical use.

title: Comparing MiniDock MTB, chest radiography, and symptoms for tuberculosis screening: a community-based evaluation in Karachi, Pakistan
abstract: Abstract Background Community-based active case finding (ACF) for tuberculosis (TB) is constrained by limited access to chest X-ray (CXR) and reliance on sputum-based diagnostic testing. Recently, WHO recommended near point-of-care testing which offers a non-sputum alternative, tongue swab (TS). We evaluated the feasibility and screening performance of MiniDock MTB on TS compared with WHO four-symptom screening (W4SS) and CXR in Pakistan. Methods We conducted 49 screening camps in underserved communities of Karachi. All adolescents and adults (> 10 years) underwent screening via W4SS, CXR, and TS collection. Individuals screening positive by any method were asked to provide sputum for Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra, sputum swab testing on MiniDock MTB, and mycobacterial culture. A microbiological reference standard (MRS) was defined as a positive Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra and/or mycobacterial culture. Results Overall, 4,303 individuals were screened (median age 28 years [IQR 16–40]); 38% were female. All participants had CXR and W4SS screening results, while 3,432 (79.8%) had valid TS results. Overall, 752 participants were screen-positive for TB, including 606 with valid TS results. TS was positive in 19/3,432 (0.4%), CXR in 302/4303 (7.0%) and W4SS in 522/4,303 (12.1%). Sputum was collected from 243 (32%) of 752 screen-positive participants, including 225 (37%) with valid TS results; Among 30 MRS-positive individuals, 29 had abnormal CXR, 14 had symptoms and 13 a positive TS result. CXR showed the highest sensitivity (96.7%; 95% CI 82.8–99.9), compared with W4SS (46.7%; 95% CI 28.3–65.7) and TS testing (46.4%; 95% CI 27.5–66.1). Conclusion TS testing, although feasible, was not sufficiently sensitive to function as a standalone TB screening test. Further optimization of specimen collection, assay performance, and evaluation in diverse settings is needed to better define the role of TS testing in community-based TB screening.

title: Longitudinal intratumoral and peritumoral MRI radiomics for predicting pathologic complete response to neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy in locally advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma: a retrospective two-center study
abstract: Abstract Background Pathologic complete response (pCR) after neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy (NACI) is an important marker of treatment sensitivity in locally advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC), but reliable preoperative prediction remains challenging. This study investigated whether longitudinal intratumoral and peritumoral MRI radiomics could improve pCR prediction and whether integration with clinicopathologic factors provided additional value. Methods This retrospective two-center study included 310 patients with locally advanced HNSCC who underwent NACI followed by definitive surgery, comprising 151 patients in the training cohort, 66 in the internal validation cohort, and 93 in the independent external test cohort. MRI was performed before treatment and after the second NACI cycle. Radiomic features were extracted from contrast-enhanced fat-suppressed T1-weighted images within the primary tumor and 1-, 3-, and 5-mm peritumoral regions. Features were selected using reproducibility assessment, correlation analysis, and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression. Pre-treatment intratumoral, on-treatment intratumoral, longitudinal intratumoral, multiscale longitudinal peritumoral, spatiotemporal radiomics, and clinical-spatiotemporal radiomics models were sequentially developed. Performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration analysis, decision curve analysis, and incremental discrimination metrics. Results Overall, 124 of 310 patients (40.0%) achieved pCR. The clinical-spatiotemporal radiomics model (M6), integrating histologic grade, combined positive score, longitudinal intratumoral features, and 3-mm longitudinal peritumoral features, showed the highest observed discrimination. The AUCs were 0.928 (95% CI, 0.882–0.974), 0.856 (95% CI, 0.749–0.963), and 0.864 (95% CI, 0.780–0.948) in the training, internal validation, and external test cohorts, respectively. In the external test cohort, sensitivity was 0.857 and specificity was 0.845. M6 also showed favorable calibration and net benefit across a broad range of threshold probabilities. Conclusions Integrating longitudinal intratumoral and peritumoral MRI radiomics with clinicopathologic factors improved preoperative prediction of pCR after NACI in locally advanced HNSCC. The model showed consistent performance in independent external testing and may support individualized pCR risk stratification, warranting further prospective multicenter validation.

title: FLNA-related periventricular nodular heterotopia with multisystem involvement: a case report
abstract: Abstract Background FLNA-related periventricular nodular heterotopia (PVNH) is an X-linked neuronal migration disorder classically associated with epilepsy. Accumulating evidence indicates that it is a multisystem disorder involving cardiac valvular, pulmonary, and ophthalmologic manifestations. We report a patient with an unusually comprehensive multisystem phenotype to emphasize the need for systematic extracranial evaluation in FLNA-related PVNH. Case presentation: A 33-year-old woman presented with two decades of headache and palpitations. Physical examination revealed digital clubbing and prominently dilated cardiac valves. Brain MRI demonstrated bilateral periventricular heterotopia. Enhanced whole-exome sequencing identified a heterozygous pathogenic nonsense variant in FLNA (NM_001110556.2:c.2193C > G, p.Tyr731Ter). Multisystem involvement comprised focal epilepsy, polyvalvular regurgitation, interstitial lung disease, and ophthalmologic abnormalities. Seizures were controlled with oxcarbazepine and lamotrigine, and the patient was referred for coordinated cardiologic, pulmonary, and ophthalmologic follow-up. Conclusions FLNA-related PVNH should be managed as a multisystem disorder rather than isolated epilepsy. Routine cardiovascular, pulmonary, and ophthalmologic screening, combined with genetic counseling for X-linked dominant transmission, should be integrated into standard care.

title: Spatial Alignment of Parkinson’s Disease-Related Quantitative MRI Alterations with Dopaminergic Topography
abstract: Abstract Objective Parkinson’s disease (PD) is characterized by a degeneration of dopaminergic neurons not only in the nigrostriatal pathways, but also in subcortical and cortical structures. Given the widespread dopaminergic innervation, PD dopamine-related dysfunction may contribute to microstructural alterations beyond the primary site of pathology. Multiparametric mapping (MPM) enables quantification of tissue biophysical properties informing the brain’s microstructure. We hypothesized that PD-related MPM alterations would show distinct spatial associations with pre- and postsynaptic dopaminergic markers. Methods 31 patients with PD and 68 healthy controls underwent a 3T MRI. We used unthresholded MPM t-maps derived from group-difference analysis to assess spatial correlation with PET-derived maps of the dopamine transporter (DAT), [ 18 F]-fluoro-L-DOPA (FDOPA), and dopamine D1 and D2 receptors. Results Proton density alterations negatively correlated with DAT (rho = 0.355, p spatial = 0.0010) and FDOPA (rho = 0.168, p FDR = 0.0080) across whole-brain gray matter. Subcortically, MPM-dopaminergic associations were structure-specific, showing concordant, same-direction associations between FDOPA and D1. Cortically, associations were more consistent, predominantly negative and driven by DAT and FDOPA. Within cortical ROIs, presupplementary and supplementary motor areas showed the most robust associations, driven by proton density (preSMA: rho = 0.428 to 0.760; SMA: rho = 0.284 to 0.789, all p FDR < 0.0001). Interpretation: PD-related microstructural-dopaminergic associations were structure- and modality-specific. Subcortically, FDOPA and D1 consistently tracked microstructural alterations, potentially reflecting coupled degeneration of dopaminergic synthesis capacity and postsynaptic receptor density. Cortically, DAT and FDOPA most robustly tracked proton density-related alterations, potentially indicating distinct and mainly neuroinflammation-driven microstructural processes beyond the primary nigrostriatal network.

title: Neuro-JEPA: Building and Evaluating Health-System Scale Neuroimaging Foundation Models with Mixture of Experts
abstract: Abstract Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the brain routinely combines complementary contrasts—including T1-weighted (T1w), T2-weighted (T2w) and FLAIR sequences—to capture anatomy and pathology. Although foundation models trained on large neuroimaging datasets have shown promise, it remains unclear whether they effectively integrate these complementary contrasts across diverse clinical settings. Here we present Neuro-JEPA, a multimodal foundation model that learns unified representations across structural brain MRIs. Neuro-JEPA combines latent predictive learning with a sparse Mixture-of-Experts architecture to encode multiple MRI contrasts within a single model. The model is pretrained on 1.55 million scans from 428,647 clinical imaging studies spanning T1w, T2w and FLAIR sequences. The model performance is evaluated on 47 downstream tasks across three independent health systems and 12 public datasets, encompassing single-contrast, multimodal and cross-domain applications. Across these evaluations, Neuro-JEPA achieved the strongest overall performance and generalized robustly across heterogeneous cohorts, outperforming existing neuroimaging foundation models and strong conventional baselines in the majority of comparisons despite using less than one-third of the pretraining data of leading models. Performance gains were particularly pronounced in data-scarce settings, reaching up to 15% over prior foundation models for clinically important pathologies including gliosis and multiple sclerosis. Neuro-JEPA showed clinically relevant capabilities across domains, including prediction of amyloid status and progression from mild cognitive impairment to Alzheimer’s disease dementia, stroke identification and classification, and prediction of post-stroke functional outcome and length of stay. Together, these results show that data scale, curation and principled model design can act synergistically to produce broadly transferable neuroimaging representations, and establish Neuro-JEPA as a scalable framework toward general-purpose multimodal foundation models for neurological imaging.

title: PSA Trends and Clinical Outcomes Following Radiotherapy Combined with Androgen Deprivation Therapy for Prostate Cancer: A Single-Centre Retrospective Cohort Study from Saudi Arabia
abstract: Abstract Background Combined external-beam radiotherapy and androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) is standard treatment for men with intermediate- to high-risk prostate cancer, but outcome data from the Gulf region remain limited despite a rising regional disease burden. We evaluated longitudinal PSA response, treatment-related morbidity, and oncological outcomes in patients treated with curative-intent radiotherapy plus ADT, characterising PSA kinetics over the first nine months of treatment and identifying clinical predictors of the PSA trajectory. Methods In this retrospective cohort study at King Abdulaziz Medical City, Riyadh, we included all adult patients with prostate cancer who received radiotherapy combined with ADT and had complete treatment and follow-up records. Demographic, clinical, and treatment data were extracted from electronic medical records, with serial PSA recorded at baseline and at 3, 6, and 9 months. Changes in PSA from baseline were assessed with the paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test, and a linear mixed-effects model (random intercept per patient; fixed effects for time, age, Gleason group, and metastatic status; PSA log₁₀[PSA + 1]-transformed) was used to identify predictors of longitudinal PSA levels. Results Seventy-four patients were included (median age 68.0 years, IQR: 63.0–75.0; median PSA at diagnosis 17.3 ng/mL, IQR: 9.3–33.0), 64.9% with Gleason group 4–5 disease. Most received hypofractionated radiotherapy (median 60 Gy in 20 fractions) with a single ADT cycle (90.4%), predominantly leuprolide (91.8%). PSA fell progressively at every interval (all p < 0.001): median reductions of 91.9%, 99.2%, and 99.7% from baseline at 3, 6, and 9 months, with the proportion achieving a ≥ 50% reduction rising from 73.2% to 93.0% over the same period; median PSA nadir was 0.028 ng/mL (IQR: 0.024–0.560). On adjusted mixed-effects modelling, reductions at each time point remained significant independent of age and Gleason group (β = −0.81 to − 1.13 versus baseline, all p < 0.001), while metastatic disease at presentation predicted higher longitudinal PSA levels. Disease recurrence occurred in 5.4% of patients, with a median time to recurrence of 68.5 months; treatment-related toxicity was low, with urinary incontinence and erectile dysfunction each affecting fewer than 7% of patients at 12 months. Conclusions In this predominantly high-risk, real-world cohort, combined radiotherapy and ADT produced rapid, deep, and durable PSA suppression with low toxicity and low biochemical recurrence, irrespective of baseline Gleason grade. These findings support the effectiveness and tolerability of this regimen outside the trial setting and provide PSA kinetic benchmarks from an underrepresented population that may complement randomised evidence, though prospective data incorporating PSMA-PET-based surveillance are needed to confirm whether early deep response translates into durable survival benefit.

title: A Pipeline for ADNI Resting-State Functional MRI Processing and Quality Control
abstract: Abstract The Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) provides a comprehensive multimodal neuroimaging resource for studying aging and Alzheimer’s disease (AD). However, its resting-state functional MRI (rs-fMRI) data remain underutilized, in part due to challenges with data processing driven by considerable variability in acquisition protocols, inconsistent organization, missing or incomplete imaging sessions, and frequency of data quality issues due to participant motion and aging-related factors. To facilitate widespread use of ADNI rs-fMRI data, we developed an open-source pipeline encompassing the download and organization of imaging and clinical data, conversion to Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS), preprocessing with fMRIPrep, and automated quality control (QC). Our QC considers acquisition parameters and 16 structural and functional MRIQC image-quality metrics, flagging scans that fall outside acceptable ranges based on expert input and robust outlier detection techniques. Processed imaging sessions are matched to temporally aligned clinical assessments to produce an analysis-ready dataset. Applying the pipeline to more than 2,800 sessions from ADNI GO, ADNI 2, and ADNI 3 yielded 2,086 quality-checked functional and structural MRI sessions from 935 unique participants. Exclusions occurred at every processing stage and were driven primarily by BIDS conversion errors, image quality flags, and preprocessing- or motion-related failures. The open-source pipeline described in this work produces one of the largest pre-processed, quality controlled, and analysis-ready functional and structural MRI datasets yet available for studying aging and AD. It lowers barriers to large-cohort and longitudinal neuroimaging research and supports large-scale neuroimaging biomarker discovery in AD.

title: Thenar Muscle Thickness Assessed by Point-of-Care Ultrasound and Geriatric Vulnerability in Hospitalized Older Adults: A Pilot Study
abstract: Abstract Background Malnutrition and sarcopenia frequently coexist in hospitalized older adults. Thenar muscle thickness (TMT) may provide a pragmatic correlate of geriatric vulnerability, but its clinical relevance is unestablished. Methods This retrospective, single-centre, cross-sectional pilot study analyzed 50 hospitalized patients aged 75 years or older, admitted between October and December 2024. Unadjusted Spearman correlations assessed associations between TMT and Mini Nutritional Assessment–Short Form (MNA-SF), Braden, and Conley scores. Bootstrap 95% confidence intervals were calculated for these three correlations. Results Mean age was 86.2 years; 60.0% of participants were women. Mean TMT was 2.62 cm (SD, 0.48). Overall, 84.0% of patients were malnourished or at risk of malnutrition, 66.0% had high pressure-injury risk, and 90.0% had a Conley score indicating fall risk. Higher TMT correlated with higher MNA-SF (rho = 0.760; 95% CI, 0.595–0.859; P < 0.001) and Braden scores (rho = 0.560; 95% CI, 0.340–0.729; P < 0.001), and with lower Conley scores (Rho = − 0.406; 95% CI, − 0.627 to − 0.141; P = 0.003). Associations remained directionally consistent after adjustment for age and sex: partial rho was 0.753 (95% CI, 0.572–0.865) for MNA-SF, 0.510 (95% CI, 0.251–0.709) for Braden, and − 0.361 (95% CI, − 0.602 to − 0.054) for Conley. TMT was not significantly associated with length of stay (Rho = − 0.240; P = 0.093). Conclusions In very old hospitalized adults, lower TMT was associated with poorer nutritional status and greater fall and pressure-injury risk. TMT may complement multidimensional geriatric assessment, but the small, unadjusted pilot design and absence of a sarcopenia reference standard preclude diagnostic or independent prognostic claims.

title: Preoperative diffusion-perivascular MRI burden and postoperative delirium after subthalamic nucleus deep brain stimulation in Parkinson disease
abstract: Abstract Postoperative delirium after subthalamic nucleus deep brain stimulation may reflect pre-existing brain vulnerability, but the preoperative imaging correlates of this vulnerability remain uncertain. We examined whether a combined diffusion and perivascular imaging burden was associated with delirium after bilateral subthalamic nucleus deep brain stimulation. This single-centre observational cohort included 100 patients with Parkinson disease undergoing bilateral subthalamic nucleus deep brain stimulation and 32 healthy controls scanned with the same preoperative MRI protocol. Delirium was assessed during postoperative days using the Nursing Delirium Screening Scale with clinical adjudication. Age- and sex-adjusted reference models fitted in healthy controls were used to standardise tract diffusion metrics, diffusion tensor image analysis along the perivascular space, and basal ganglia enlarged perivascular space counts. Directionally aligned diffusion and perivascular scores were averaged with equal domain weights. Patients who developed postoperative delirium (n = 30) had higher combined burden than those who did not (n = 70; 95% CI, 0.584 to 1.526; q<.001). Using Firth penalised logistic regression, higher combined burden remained associated with postoperative delirium after adjustment for age, sex, education, Mini-Mental State Examination score, disease duration, and motor severity (95% CI, 1.49 to 4.25; Wald P<.001). Higher burden was also associated with longer delirium duration and higher peak screening scores among affected patients. Exploratory internal prediction yielded an area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve of 0.701 after adding burden to clinical variables, compared with 0.538 for clinical variables alone. These findings support preoperative diffusion-perivascular burden as a candidate marker of perioperative neuropsychiatric vulnerability requiring multicentre validation.

title: Transthoracic echocardiography for initial screening of single coronary artery anomaly: a case with multimodal imaging evaluation
abstract: Abstract Single coronary artery anomaly (SCA) is a rare congenital coronary malformation with only one aortic coronary ostium supplying the whole myocardium. Clinical outcomes mainly depend on the anatomical course of the aberrant vessel. We report a 73-year-old female presenting with intermittent precordial chest pain. Transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) revealed a dilated right coronary artery (RCA) with normal ostial location, non-visualization of the left coronary artery ostium, and diastolic low-resistance arterial flow signal within the interventricular septum along the expected left anterior descending artery (LAD) territory. Coronary computed-tomography angiography (CCTA) demonstrated right-dominant coronary circulation, absence of the native left coronary artery, and an abnormally extended posterior descending artery travelling into the anterior interventricular groove. Multimodal imaging highly suggested Lipton-Yamanaka type R-I SCA. The patient received conservative medical therapy for co-existing mild coronary atherosclerosis. This case underlines TTE as a valuable first-line screening tool for congenital coronary anomalies. Nevertheless, definitive subtyping requires CCTA or invasive coronary angiography.

title: Agreement of Radiographic Parameters Between Digitally Reconstructed Radiographs from Weight-Bearing Cone-Beam CT and Whole-Spine Radiographs
abstract: Abstract Purpose Current spinal deformity diagnosis relies on whole-spine radiographs, while Weight-bearing Radiology 3D (WR3D) offers accurate, low-dose three-dimensional reconstruction in the standing position. This study aims to evaluate the potential of digitally reconstructed radiographs (DRRs) generated from WR3D images as a substitute for standard whole-spine radiographs. Methods In this retrospective comparative study of 67 patients who underwent both WR3D examination and whole-spine radiographs, DRRs were generated using segmentation and projection algorithms. Two observers independently measured coronal and sagittal radiographic parameters of the spine and pelvis on both imaging modalities, with intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) calculated. Paired samples t -tests and Bland-Altman analyses were performed, with mean absolute errors (MAEs) and Pearson correlation coefficients calculated. Results DRRs exhibited superior interobserver reliability compared to radiographs, particularly for pelvic incidence (PI, ICC = 0.95 vs. 0.70), pelvic tilt (PT, ICC = 0.98 vs. 0.83), sacral slope (SS, ICC = 0.94 vs. 0.79), and upper thoracic parameters. High agreement between the two imaging modalities was observed in measurements of all coronal parameters, cervical lordosis (C2-C7), thoracolumbar kyphosis (T10-L2), lumbar lordosis (L4-S1, L1-S1), PI, and PT ( p > 0.05), while differences were observed for other sagittal parameters ( p < 0.05). Conclusions DRR images based on WR3D show high agreement with radiographs for measuring most structural parameters. However, certain differences exist for global balance parameters and sagittal curvature parameters.
